sense.def: A city, capital, and municipality of North Brabant, Netherlands.
A possessive marker, indicating that an object belongs to the noun or noun phrase bearing the marker.
Able to be done; fit to be done.
An action or process.
The result of an action or process.
an immature cell or tissue
Used to make the names of hamburgers served in buns with the addition of the specified foodstuff, or with that foodstuff used in place of the usual meat.
(anime and manga fandom) Appended to a person's name (usually a female, child, a close friend, or an intimate) to add politeness. It is sometimes used to denote cuteness or familiarity.
killing
killer
Used to form past tenses of (regular) verbs. In linguistics, it is used for the base form of any past form. See -t for a variant.
Used to form possessional adjectives from nouns, in the sense of having the object represented by the noun.
Added to transitive verbs to form words meaning a person or thing that is the object of that verb (i.e., to whom or to which an action is done).
(added to verbs) A person or thing that does an action indicated by the root verb; used to form an agent noun.
(added to certain adjectives and adverbs, now especially short ones) More; used to form the comparative.
(added to a proper noun) Suffix denoting a resident or inhabitant of (the place denoted by the proper noun); used to form a demonym.
In the style or manner of; appended to nouns, especially proper nouns, and forming adjectives.
Used to form the superlative of adjectives and adverbs.
(Internet slang, originally, _, 4chan, offensive, derogatory) Suffix that forms pejorative nouns, generally referring to specific types of people and sometimes used ironically or even affectionately.
Used to make adjectives meaning times.
A producer of something, or an agent in the production of something.
(geometry) Forms the names of plane figures containing a given number of internal angles, and thus bounded by that number of line segments (polygons).
An adjective suffix, now usually in a passive sense; forms adjectives meaning "able to be", "relevant or suitable to, in accordance with", or expressing capacity or worthiness in a passive sense.

(chemistry) Used to denote certain chemical compounds in which a specified chemical element has a higher oxidation number than in the equivalent compound whose name ends in the suffix -ous. For example sulphuric acid (H₂SO₄) has more oxygen atoms per molecule than sulphurous acid (H₂SO₃).
Forms nouns referring to fields of knowledge or practice.
Any of a group of related compounds - azide, polysaccharide, glycoside.
Forms nouns denoting the act or process whereby a subject becomes something else.
Forms transitive verbs meaning "to make" from adjectives and nouns.
Related through marriage.
Used to form present participles of verbs.
Used to form nouns denoting materials or systems of objects which are used or employed in an action, or considered collectively.
(of adjectives from common nouns) Typical of, similar to, being like.
Used to form names of a tendency of action, behaviour, condition, opinion, or state belonging to a class or group of persons, or the result of a doctrine, ideology, or principle or lack thereof.
one who subscribes to a particular theological doctrine or religious denomination;
a person who speaks or specializes in a (usually constructed) language.
(chemistry) Used to form names of certain chemical compounds, especially salts or esters of acids whose name ends in -ous.
(pathology) Denoting diseases characterized by inflammation, itself often caused by an infection.
Used to forms nouns of state, condition or quality.
Used to form an uncountable noun from an adjective; especially, to form the noun referring to the state, property, or quality of conforming to the adjective's description.
An adjective suffix signifying relating or belonging to, of the nature of, tending to, or serving to; as: affirmative, active, conclusive, corrective, diminutive.
Forms nouns denoting the act, process, or result of doing/making what is denoted by the noun/adjective.
Used to form verbs from nouns or adjectives, especially similative verbs
(anime and manga fandom) Appended to a young man's name or nickname to indicate familiarity.
Used to form the name of a territory, country, or region.
Lacking (something); without (something). Added usually to a noun to form an adjective signifying a lack of that noun.
Resembling, having some of the characteristics of (used to form adjectives from nouns).
small, immature, miniature
A person who studies or is an expert in the related -logy.
A branch of learning; a study of a particular subject.
Used to form adverbs from adjectives and nouns.
Used to form the names of measuring devices.
Marks ordinals written in digits when the final term of the spelled number is "second"
Appended to adjectives to form nouns meaning "the state of being (the adjective)", "the quality of being (the adjective)", or "the measure of being (the adjective)".
(often, humorous) added to an ordinary English word to create a name for a (possibly non-existent) field of study.
(physics, maths) Forming nouns denoting subatomic particles and quanta.
(pathology) functional disease or condition such as hepatosis

(chemistry) Used in chemical nomenclature to name chemical compounds in which a specified chemical element has a lower oxidation number than in the equivalent compound whose name ends in the suffix -ic. For example sulphuric acid (H2SO4) has more oxygen atoms per molecule than sulphurous acid (H2SO3). See Inorganic nomenclature.
(pathology) Used to form nouns meaning abnormal liking or tendency (for something), e.g. paraphilia.
Used to form nouns meaning fear of a specific thing.
Used to form nouns meaning hate, dislike, or repression of a specific thing.
Forming nouns: a speaker of a certain language.
Suffix added to a noun to form an adjective denoting imperviousness to that noun.
Marks ordinals written in digits when the final term of the spelled number is "third"
Used to form regular plurals of nouns.
(anime, _, and, _, manga, fandom) Appended to a person's name or nickname to convey honour and respect.
(informal, mostly, Japanophilic slang) Honorific ending used to indicate that a person is Japanese, talking with a Japanese, or treated like a Japanese.
Marks ordinals written in digits when the final term of the spelled number is "first"
Used to form cardinal numbers from thirteen to nineteen.
(mathematics) Used to form a term denoting the ordinal numeral corresponding to the value, being a natural number, of a mathematical expression.

(non-productive) Used to form nouns meaning "the action of (a verb)" or "the result of (a verb)". Words ending in this suffix are almost always derived from a similar Latin word; a few (e.g. gumption) are not derived from Latin and are unrelated to any verb. More often, -ation is used.
Cutting, incision, section
(mathematics) A tuple containing the specified number of terms.
A nonproductive suffix indicating single-digit integer multiples of ten.
Denotes singular grammatical number.
One at a time, or one thing at a time.
Added to nouns and adjectives to form adjectives meaning “having the quality of”, either “involving the referent” or “analogous to it”.
Forming familiar names, pet names, nicknames and terms of endearment.

(computing, Microsoft) A set of Microsoft products and services – primarily the .NET Framework, which permits the development of software for a virtual machine in any programming language that is CLI-compliant (i.e., conforms with the Common Language Infrastructure).
(biblical) The first of the two Books of Chronicles and the thirteenth book of the Old Testament of the Bible.

A timekeeping convention in which the 24 hours of the day are treated as a single period rather than two sets of 12 hours, with the result that midnight is indicated as 00:00 (or sometimes 24:00), and the hours from 1:00 to 11:00 p.m. as 13:00 to 23:00.
A menial blue-collar job often performed by migrants.
(printing) A device for making three-dimensional solid objects from a digital model.

(sports) A coach-less (no in-game coaching) form of basketball, with 2 opposing sides of 3 on-court players at a time on a side, on a court with a single basket, half the size of a regular basketball court, where defenders and attackers switch during play.
(athletics) A sprint race over 400 metres.
(geometry) A four-dimensional polytope, analogous to a tetrahedron, whose five bounding facets are tetrahedra.
(athletics) A long-distance running race over 5000 metres.
Any of the six basic question words in English, with 5 of them beginning with “w” (what, when, where, who, why) and 1 of them beginning with “h” (how).
(geometry) A four-dimensional polytope, analogous to an icosahedron, whose 600 bounding facets are tetrahedra.

In Latin grammar, the ablative case (cāsus ablātīvus) includes functions derived from the Indo-European ablative, instrumental, comitative, associative and locative cases; these cases express concepts similar to those of the English prepositions "of"/"from", "by", "with", "to"/"with", and "at"/"in", respectively. (games) Any of the many games played with playing cards.
(computing) A data input device that reads data from a card-shaped storage medium.
An herb, native to India (Elettaria cardamomum.
(uncommon, inexact) , seeds or seed capsules of Aframomum melegueta, of East Africa.
A wood-based material resembling heavy paper, used in the manufacture of boxes, cartons and signs.
An industrially prefabricated box made from cardboard, primarily used for packaging goods or materials and often recycled.
A corrugated box.
(Cockney rhyming slang) Syphilis.
(slang, derogatory, uncommon) Someone who is very dull and uninteresting.
(anatomy) The area of the stomach which directly receives contents from the esophagus.
(cardiology, pathology) The sudden and complete cessation of the heartbeat resulting in the loss of effective circulation of the blood.
A type of sweater or jumper that fastens up the front with buttons or a zipper, usually machine- or hand-knitted from wool.
Of fundamental importance; crucial, pivotal.
Describing a “natural” number used to indicate quantity (e.g., zero, one, two, three), as opposed to an ordinal number indicating relative position.
(Roman Catholic) One of the officials appointed by the pope in the Roman Catholic Church, ranking only below the pope, equal to the patriarchs, constituting the special college which elects the pope.

Any of various species of New-World passerine songbird in the genus Cardinalis, or in the family Cardinalidae more generally, or of similar appearance and once considered to be related to the former; so called because of their red plumage. (See Wikipedia article for taxonomical information.)
A deep red color, somewhat less vivid than scarlet, the traditional colour of a Catholic cardinal's cassock. (same as cardinal red)
(math) Ellipsis of cardinal number, a number indicating quantity, or the size of a set (e.g., 0, 1, 2, 3). (See Cardinal_number.)
A number used to denote quantity; a counting number; a cardinal.
(mathematics) A generalized kind of number used to denote the size of a set, including infinite sets.
(grammar) A word used to represent a cardinal number.
Any of the four principal points of the compass: north, south, east and west.
(set theory, of a set) The number of elements a given set contains.
A physician who specializes in medical problems related to the heart.
(medicine) The study of the structure, function, and disorders of the heart.
(pathology) The deterioration of the myocardium.
(medicine) Of or pertaining to both the heart and the lungs.
A first aid procedure for cardiac arrest involving compression of the chest wall alternating with artificial respiration.
Relating to the circulatory system, that is the heart and blood vessels.
A disease involving the heart or blood vessels, i.e. arteries and veins, such as coronary heart disease.
Close attention; concern; responsibility.
(transitive, intransitive) To be concerned (about), to have an interest (in); to feel concern (about).
(intransitive) (with for) To look after or look out for.
(mail) For distribution by (the named intermediary).
One’s calling in life; one's working occupation or profession, especially when pursued seriously and/or over a long period of time.
(This entry is a translation hub.)
A woman who is dedicated to her career.
Without cares or worries; free of concern or worries; without difficulty.
Conscientious and painstaking; meticulous.
With care; attentively, circumspectly.
Not giving sufficient attention or thought, especially concerning the avoidance of harm or mistakes. [from 16thc.]
Giving the appearance of carelessness; relaxedly.
Lack of care; the state or quality of being careless.
(chiefly, UK, Ireland, Commonwealth) Someone who regularly looks after another person, either as a job or often through family responsibilities.
A gentle stroking or rubbing.
(transitive) To touch or kiss lovingly; to fondle.
Freight carried by a ship, aircraft, or motor vehicle.

Any of several religious movements among the people of Melanesia that anticipate the arrival of material cargo or cultural restoration, typically through the ritual imitation of the activities of colonial or technological cultures.
A ship that carries cargo.
Any of several North American subspecies Rangifer tarandus of the reindeer.
Having the characteristics of a caricature, grotesque.
The progressive destruction of bone or tooth by decay.
(musical instrument) A set of bells, often in a bell tower, sometimes operated by means of a keyboard (manual or pedal), originating from the Low Countries.
(transitive) To steal an automobile forcibly from (someone).
(mineral) A rare oxide mineral discovered in 2019, with the chemical formula ZrAl2Ti4O11.
Death and destruction.
(botany) A type of Eurasian plant widely cultivated for its flowers.
The type of flower they bear, originally flesh-coloured, but since hybridizing found in a variety of colours.
(organic compound) A betaine, 3-hydroxy-4-trimethylammonio-butanoate, that is found in the liver and has a function in fatty acid transport.
A festive occasion marked by parades and sometimes special foods and other entertainment.
An organism that feeds chiefly on animals; an animal that feeds on meat as the main part of its diet.
(zoology) A mammal belonging to the order Carnivora.
Predatory or flesh-eating.
An evergreen shrub or tree, Ceratonia siliqua, native to the Mediterranean region.
The fruit of that tree.
A ballad or song of joy.
(organic chemistry) A class of tetraterpene plant pigments; they vary in colour from yellow, through orange to red, this colour originating in a chain of alternating single and double bonds.
(organic chemistry) Any of a class of yellow to red organic pigments including the carotenes and xanthophylls.
(anatomy) .
Any of various freshwater fish of the family Cyprinidae; specifically the common carp, Cyprinus carpio.
Enjoy the present, make the most of today, (common mistranslation) seize the day.

(botany) A constituent part of a flower pistil: the female reproductive organs in a flower. A carpel is composed of an ovary, a style, and a stigma, although some flowers have carpels without a distinct style. In origin, carpels are leaves (megasporophylls) that have evolved to enclose the ovules. A pistil may be composed of a single carpel or of several carpels fused together.
A person skilled at carpentry, the trade of cutting and joining timber in order to construct buildings or other structures.

(nautical) A senior rating in ships responsible for all the woodwork onboard; in the days of sail, a warrant officer responsible for the hull, masts, spars and boats of a ship, and whose responsibility was to sound the well to see if the ship was making water.
(zoology) A carpenter bee.
A bee of the subfamily Xylocopinae, that burrows in dead wood.
A tool used to measure out right angles.
A fabric used as a complete floor covering.
A tool for beating dust out of carpets, cushions, etc., used in housecleaning before the invention of the vacuum cleaner.
Large area bombardment done in a progressive manner to inflict damage in every part of a selected area of land.
An arrangement whereby several people travel together in the same car in order to save costs, reduce pollution etc.
(historical) A large European sailing vessel of the 14th to 17th centuries similar to a caravel but square-rigged on the foremast and mainmast and lateen-rigged on the mizzenmast.
(by extension) A cubicle or partitioned space for reading or studying, often in a library.
A (mostly four-wheeled) lighter vehicle chiefly designed to transport people, generally drawn by horse power.
(UK, Ireland, Hong Kong) The part of a road that carries traffic.
(UK) A bag made of thin polythene or paper, generally used for carrying groceries or other purchased items.
A domestic pigeon which transports attached messages or very small parcels from the place where it is released to a familiar destination.
(physics) A wave that can be modulated, either in amplitude, frequency, or phase, to carry or transmit images, music, speech, or other signals.
Rotting flesh of a dead animal or person.
The common European black crow Corvus corone.
A vegetable with a nutritious, juicy, sweet root that is often orange in colour, Daucus carota, family Apiaceae, especially the subspecies sativus.
(idiomatic) The simultaneous rewarding of good behavior and punishing of bad behavior.
(Singapore) Turnip cake; radish cake (a savoury cake containing radish, usually pan-fried).
(transitive) To lift (something) and take it to another place; to transport (something) by lifting.
(idiomatic) To do something that is unneeded or redundant.
(transitive) To execute or perform; to put into operation; to do.
A yoke of wood or bamboo, used by people to carry a load.
Motion sickness caused by riding in a motor car.
A small, open, wheeled vehicle, drawn or pushed by a person or animal, often with two wheels on one axle, more often used for transporting goods than passengers.
A small motor vehicle resembling a car; a go-cart.
Unlimited discretionary power to act; unrestricted authority.
(economics) A group of businesses or nations that collude to limit competition within an industry or market.

(skeleton, uncountable) A usually translucent and somewhat elastic, dense, nonvascular connective tissue found in various forms in the larynx and respiratory tract, in structures such as the external ear, and in the articulating surfaces of joints. It composes most of the skeleton of vertebrate embryos, being replaced by bone during ossification in the higher vertebrates.
One who makes maps or charts.
(uncountable) The creation of charts and maps based on the layout of a territory's geography. [from 19th c.]
Fortune-telling using cards, as in tarot and Lenormand.
An inexpensive, disposable box-like container fashioned from either paper, paper with wax-covering (wax paper), or other lightweight material.
(comics) A humorous drawing, often with a caption, or a strip of such drawings.
(animation) A cartoon series.
(comics) One who creates a cartoon or strip cartoon.
(architectural element) An ornamental figure, often on an oval shield.
(Egyptology, hieroglyphs) An oval figure containing the characters of an important personal name, such as that of royal or divine people.
(firearms) The package consisting of the bullet, primer, and casing containing gunpowder; a round of ammunition.
(computing) A vessel which contains the ink or toner for a computer printer and can be easily replaced with another.
The act or craft of producing a carved object.
A large knife designed for cutting cooked turkey and similar dishes.
(botany) A type of fruit in which the fruit skin is stuck to the seed coat; especially the grain of a cereal.
The fortress in a city in North Africa or the Middle East.
An actual event, situation, or fact.
A box that contains or can contain a number of identical items of manufacture.
A piece of work, specifically defined within a profession; the set of tasks involved in addressing the situation of a specific person or event.
(medicine) An instance of a specific condition or set of symptoms.
(academia) An instance or event as a topic of study.
A suitcase.
The outer covering or framework of a piece of apparatus such as a computer.
Used other than figuratively or idiomatically: see A case is closed; specifically, a police investigation or similar is resolved.
(uncountable) Research performed in detail on a single individual, group, incident or community, as opposed to, for instance, a sample of the whole population.
(protein) A protein present in both milk and in the seeds of leguminous plants
(pathology) A form of cell death in which the tissue maintains a cheese-like appearance.
A place in a restaurant, bar, or shop etc, typically containing a cash register, where a customer can pay the bill.

cit.quote: キャッシュレジスター

sense.def: A machine that tabulates the amount of sales transactions, makes a permanent and cumulative record of them, and has a drawer in which cash can be kept.
A book used to record amounts of money received or paid out.
A tree, Anacardium occidentale, native to northeastern Brazil, now widely grown in tropical climates for its cashew nuts and cashew apples.
The seed of the cashew tree, often viewed as a nut in the culinary sense.
One who works at a till or receives payments.
(mostly, uncountable) Fine, downy wool from beneath the outer hair of the Cashmere goat.
(mostly, uncountable) A soft fabric made of this wool.
That which encloses or encases.
A public building or room for gambling.
A large barrel for the storage of liquid, especially of alcoholic drinks. (See a diagram of cask sizes.)
A helmet.
A rich cake, typical of Sicily, containing liqueur layered with ricotta, candied fruit and chocolate.
Manioc (Manihot esculenta), a tropical plant which is the source of tapioca.
(countable) A dish of glass or earthenware, with a lid, in which food is baked and sometimes served.
Food, such as a stew, cooked in such a dish.
A small flat case containing magnetic tape on two reels, used to record and play back audio and video material.
(mineral) A generally black mineral, composed of tin oxide, SnO2, which is an important ore of tin.
An item of clerical clothing: a long, sheath-like, close-fitting, ankle-length robe worn by clergy members of some Christian denominations. [from 17th c.]
Any large flightless bird of the genus Casuarius that is native to Australia and New Guinea, has a characteristic bony crest on its head, and can be very dangerous.
(art) The collective group of actors performing a play or production together. Contrasted with crew.
A supportive and immobilising device used to help mend broken bones.
To turn (the balance or scale); to overbalance; hence, to make preponderate; to decide.
To shape (molten metal etc.) by pouring into a mould; to make (an object) in such a way. [from 15th c.]
A hard and brittle, but strong, alloy of iron, carbon, and silicon, formed by casting in a mould.
A (usually weighted) fishing net that is thrown and then pulled back by means of an attached line.
(musical instruments, chiefly, in the plural) A single handheld percussion instrument consisting of a pair of concave shells or shell-shaped parts joined on one edge by string.
Any of the hereditary social classes and subclasses of South Asian societies or similar found historically in other cultures.
A Japanese sponge cake made of sugar, flour, eggs, and starch syrup.
(chiefly, _, historical) The governor or caretaker entrusted to oversee a castle or keep for its lord.
A shaker with a perforated top for sprinkling condiments such as sugar, salt, pepper, etc.
(automotive) The angle of the axis around which a car's front wheels rotate when the steering wheel is turned, with a vertical axis being defined as zero caster.
The act or process of selecting actors, singers, dancers, models, etc.
(hunting) Of hounds, the act of spreading out and searching for a scent.
A vote made by the leader or chair of a group, in the event of a deadlock

A large residential building or compound that is fortified and contains many defences; in previous ages often inhabited by a nobleman or king. Also, a house or mansion with some of the architectural features of medieval castles.
(chess) A move in which the king moves two squares towards a rook, and the rook moves to the other side of the king; the action of the verb to castle.
Seed of the castor oil plant, used in the production of castor oil and of the poison ricin.
A tick of species Ixodes ricinus, a vector for Lyme disease and tick-borne encephalitis.
The pale yellow vegetable oil extracted from the castor bean; used as a laxative and an industrial lubricant.
A plant of the species Ricinus communis, used in the production of castor oil and of the poison ricin.
(transitive) To remove the testicles of a person or animal.
(surgery) The act of removing the testicles.
(figuratively) Any act that removes power from a person (particularly a man) or entity.
Causing (the effects of) castration.
A male who has been castrated, especially a male whose testicles have been removed before puberty in order to retain his boyish voice.
A male soprano or alto voice produced by castration of the treble singer before puberty, intended to conserve his voice; the singer.
One who castrates (gelds or neuters).
Happening by chance.
Coming without regularity; occasional or incidental.
Employed irregularly.
Happening or coming to pass without design.
(of behavior, usage, or milieu) Informal; relaxed.
(of clothing or utensils) Designed for informal or everyday use.
Sexual activity that is undertaken without commitment, emotional attachment or personal familiarity between the participants involved.
(military) A person in military service who becomes unavailable for duty, for any reason (notably death, injury, illness, capture, or desertion).
An act seen as justifying or causing a war; an act of war.
(countable, by extension) Chiefly with a descriptive word: an animal not of the family Felidae which (somewhat) resembles a domestic feline (sense 1.1.1).
Any similar, chiefly non-domesticated, animal of the family Felidae, which includes bobcats, caracals, cheetahs, cougars, leopards, lions, lynxes, tigers, and other such species.
(countable) An animal of the family Felidae.
A carnivorous, four-legged, generally furry domesticated species (Felis catus) of feline animal, commonly kept as a house pet. [from 8th c.]
A relationship in which two parties closely monitor and challenge one another in a suspicious or self-protective manner, often because each party is attempting to gain an advantage over the other.
A children's game in which one player (the "cat") attempts to break through a ring of players to catch another player (the "mouse") in the centre.
A particularly stealthy burglar, especially one who gains undetected entry through the use of agility.
A café that has domestic cats with which the clientele can interact.
A small, hinged panel, usually cut into a door, with an opening just large enough for a cat to enter.
A type of food specially formulated for the feeding of cats, typically composed of processed grain and meat byproducts as dry food or canned fish or meat as wet food.
(informal, sometimes, derogatory) A woman, often elderly, who devotes her time and attention to one or usually many domestic cats.
(medicine) A relatively benign disease, characterized by swollen lymph nodes, caused by the bacterium Bartonella henselae normally carried by the cat flea Ctenocephalides felis.
A structure of platforms and scratching posts designed for a cat to play on.
An exercise wheel used by cats.
(uncountable) A children's game of forming string into various shapes around one's fingers.
(countable, especially, Commonwealth, usually, _, in the plural) A retroreflective device placed on a road surface as a marking that can be seen even at night.
A small chocolate bar or (sometimes chocolate-covered) cookie/biscuit which is shaped somewhat like the tongue of a cat.
(biochemistry) Destructive (lytic) metabolism or metabolization, usually including the release of energy and breakdown of materials.
A misuse of a word; an application of a term to something which it does not properly denote.
A sudden, violent event.
(geology) A sudden and violent change in the earth's crust.
A great flood.
(often plural) An underground system of tunnels and chambers with recesses for graves, used (in former times) as a cemetery; a tunnel system used for burying the dead, as in Paris or Ancient Rome.
(pathology) A severe bodily condition, described in psychiatric pathology, marked by sudden rigidity, fixation of posture, and loss of contact with environmental conditions.
A systematic list of books, names, pictures, etc.
(chemistry) The increase of the rate of a chemical reaction, induced by a catalyst.
(chemistry) A substance that increases the rate of a chemical reaction without being consumed in the process.
A twin-hulled ship or boat.
A boy or younger man in a homoerotic relationship with an older man. [1552]
(military, historical) Defensive armour covering the entire body of a soldier and often the soldier's horse as well, especially the linked mail or scale armour of some eastern nations.
(military, historical) A soldier (especially a horseman) covered with a cataphract (etymology 1, sense 1).
(medicine) An abrupt loss of muscle tone, sometimes associated with narcolepsy.
A device or weapon for throwing or launching large objects.
(ophthalmology, pathology) A clouding of the lens in the eye leading to a decrease in vision.
(mechanics, chiefly, historical) A type of governor used in single-acting steam engines, where a flow of water through an opening regulates the stroke.
Any large and disastrous event of great significance.

A severe psychiatric condition, often associated with schizophrenia, characterized by a tendency to remain in a rigid state of stupor for long periods which give way to short periods of extreme agitation.
(uncountable) The game of catching a ball.
(countable, cricket, baseball) The act of catching a hit ball before it reaches the ground, resulting in an out.
(transitive) To capture or snare (someone or something which would rather escape). [from 13thc.]
(transitive) To entrap or trip up a person; to deceive. [from 14thc.]
(intransitive) To engage with some mechanism; to stick, to succeed in interacting with something or initiating some process.
(transitive, surfing) To contact a wave in such a way that one can ride it back to shore.
(transitive) To seize or intercept an object moving through the air (or, sometimes, some other medium). [from 16thc.]
(transitive) To grasp mentally: perceive and understand. [from 16thc.]
(idiomatic) To contract a cold.
(idiomatic) To become engulfed in flames, to combust.
to take in a breath sharply and hold it, usually in reaction to a sudden shock, or surprise
(transitive) To discover or capture someone in the act of committing a crime.
(ambitransitive) To reach something that had been ahead.
(baseball) The player who squats behind home plate and receives the pitches from the pitcher.
A repeated expression, often originating in popular culture.
(of a tune or phrase) Instantly appealing and memorable.
A book, in question and answer form, summarizing the basic principles of Christianity.
A convert to Christianity under instruction before baptism; a young or recent Christian preparing for confirmation.
Absolute; having no exception.
Of, pertaining to, or using a category or categories.
In a categorical manner.
(transitive) To assign a category; to divide into classes.
A group, often named or numbered, to which items are assigned based on similarity or defined criteria.

(mathematics) A collection of objects, together with a transitively closed collection of composable arrows between them, such that every object has an identity arrow, and such that arrow composition is associative.

(mathematics) A branch of mathematics which deals with spaces and maps between them in abstraction, taking similar theorems from various disparate more concrete branches of mathematics and unifying them.

(engineering) Any physical cable, rope, chain, or other weight-supporting structure taking such geometric shape, as a suspension cable for a bridge or a power-transmission line or an arch for a bridge or roof.
(cards, dice, obsolete) The four of cards or dice.
(US, Canada) Diagonally across from.
(uncountable, UK, Philippines) The business of providing food and related services; foodservice.
The larva of a butterfly or moth; leafworm.
A vehicle with a caterpillar track; a crawler.
especially, species Ophiocordyceps sinensis, indigenous to the Tibetan plateau.

A generic trademark name for a continuous track in the form of a steel or rubber belt fitted around the wheels of crawlers, bulldozers, excavators, loaders, backhoes, tanks and similar off-road vehicles in such a manner as to spread the load on the ground surface and thereby improve traction and reduce sinking into soft surfaces.
(slang) A fight or bickering, especially between women.
The meat of such a fish, popular in the Southern U.S. and Central Europe.
(Japanese fiction) A female fictional character who has a cat's ears, tail, or other feline characteristics on an otherwise humanoid body.

(drama) A release of emotional tension after an overwhelming vicarious experience, resulting in the purging or purification of the emotions, as through watching a dramatic production (especially a tragedy).
Any release of emotional tension to the same effect, more widely.
The principal church serving as the office (and some as place of residence) of an archdiocese's/a diocese's archbishop/bishop which is symbolized by an episcopal throne known as the cathedra.
(loosely or informally) A large or important church building.
(medicine) A small tube inserted into a body cavity to administer a drug, create an opening, distend a passageway, or remove fluid.
(geometry) A line perpendicular to a surface (or line); in particular, either of the sides of a right triangle other than its hypotenuse.

(electricity) An electrode, of a cell or other electrically polarized device, through which a positive current of electricity flows outwards (and thus, electrons flow inwards). It can have either a negative or a positive voltage with respect to anode of the same polarized device (depending on whether the device is a load or a source, respectively).

(electronics) A vacuum tube that displays still or moving images (such as for a television), by controlling the direction of a cathode ray emitted towards the front of the tube. The front is coated by a layer of fluorescent material, so that it emits light when struck by the beam.
(Christianity) A high-ranking bishop or patriarch in certain Eastern Christian traditions.
(botany) A type of inflorescence, consisting of an axis with many unisexual apetalous flowers along its sides, as in the willow and poplar.
(slang) The loaflike form of a domestic cat sitting with its paws and tail tucked underneath its body.
Any of the about 250 species of flowering plant of the genus Nepeta, family Lamiaceae, certain of which are said to have medicinal qualities.
Nepeta cataria and Nepeta grandiflora (and perhaps other species), which are well-known for causing an apparently harmless pheromone-based intoxication among certain cats.
A legendary creature from Ethiopia, said to have the body of a Cape buffalo, scales on its back, and the head of a wild boar, which always points downward because of its weight.
(US, historically, Yorkshire, Lincolnshire) Any of several perennial herbs, of the genus Typha, that have long flat leaves, and grow in marshy places.
Certain other livestock, such as sheep, pigs or goats. Also rarely applied to horses.
(pejorative, figuratively) People who resemble domesticated bovine animals in behavior or destiny.
A man who raises or tends cattle, as:
A (unit of) weight used in China which is metricated in Mainland China as exactly 0.5 kg, and approximately 0.6 kg for other places.
(fashion) A narrow elevated stage on which models parade.
A Catalan sweet made from almonds coated in caramel and powdered chocolate.
A grouping of all the members of a legislature from the same party.
A political interest group by members of a legislative body.
(anatomy) A bundle of nerve roots at the base of the spinal column
(zoology) Pertaining to the tail or posterior or hind part of a body.
The tailfin of a fish and other aquatic vertebrates.
(neuroanatomy) a nucleus within each hemisphere of the brain, sitting astride the thalamus and located near the center of the brain.
(historical) A style of close-fitting circular cap worn by women in the sixteenth century and later, often made of linen. [from 14th c.]
A large bowl-shaped pot used for boiling over an open flame.
Brassica oleracea var. botrytis, an annual variety of cabbage, of which the cluster of young flower stalks and buds is eaten as a vegetable.
The edible head or curd of a cauliflower plant.
of, relating to, or being a cause of something; causing
The agency of a cause; the action or power of a cause, in producing its effect.
(grammar) Expressing a cause#Noun or causation#Noun.
(grammar) An expression of an agent causing or forcing a patient to perform an action (or to be in a certain condition).
(countable, often with of, typically of adverse results) The source of, or reason for, an event or action; that which produces or effects a result.
(countable) A goal, aim or principle, especially one which transcends purely selfish ends.
(transitive) To set off an event or action; to bring about; to produce.
Causation; causality; the process whereby a cause leads to an effect.
The official cause of a human death as typically determined by a coroner during an autopsy and included on the death certificate of a deceased person.

A road that is raised so as to be above water, marshland, and similar low-lying obstacles, which in some cases may flood periodically (e.g. due to tides). Originally causeways were much like dykes, generally pierced to let water through, whereas many modern causeways are more like bridges or viaducts.
sodium hydroxide (NaOH), a strong alkaline substance used in the manufacture of paint, soap and detergents, or as a drain cleaner.
To burn and hence seal open tissue using a heated article or caustic agent so as to stop bleeding or minimise the risk of infection.
A careful attention to the probable effects of an act, in order that failure or harm may be avoided.
(collective) A procession of riders, vehicles, ships, etc.
(historical) A gallant: a sprightly young dashing military man.
(military, usually, _, historical, uncountable) The military arm of service that fights while riding horses.
A type of pasta, with rolled edges.
A large, naturally-occurring cavity formed underground or in the face of a cliff or a hillside.
To collapse inward or downward.
An early human or closely related species, popularly held to reside in caves.
Roe of the sturgeon or of certain other large fish, considered a delicacy.
(fluid dynamics) The formation, in a fluid, of vapor bubbles that rapidly collapse, especially in a rotating marine propeller or pump impeller.
A hole or hollow depression in a solid object.
(anatomy) A hollow area within the body.
(dentistry) A small or large hole in a tooth caused by caries; often also a soft area adjacent to the hole also affected by caries.
A rendering of the vocalisation of a crow or other corvid.
Any of several very hot chilli peppers.
A powder condiment or spice formed from the dried chilli pepper varieties above.
(formal, intransitive) To stop.
(formal, transitive) To stop doing (something).
(legal) To stop and not resume an action.
In warfare, an agreed end to hostilities for a specific purpose. (Typically only temporary).
(countable) A coniferous tree of the genus Cedrus in the family Pinaceae.
A medium-sized passerine bird native to North and Central America (Bombycilla cedrorum).
(transitive) To give up; yield to another. [with to]

(orthography) In the spelling of Catalan, French, Portuguese and some other languages, a mark ⟨¸⟩ sometimes placed under the letter c to indicate that it is pronounced /s/ rather than /k/, as in Catalan força, French menaçant, and Portuguese almoço, and also used in various other languages to change the sounds of other letters.
The name of the Latin-script letter C/c.
(mathematics) The smallest integer greater than or equal to a given number.
(architecture) The overhead interior surface that covers the upper limits of a room.
A pale green colour, possibly tinted with gray.
A pale green Chinese glaze.
A ceramic ware with a pale green glaze.
(informal) A celebrity; a famous person, a one who is celebrated.
(transitive) To extol or honour in a solemn manner.
(transitive) To honour by rites, by ceremonies of joy and respect, or by refraining from ordinary business; to observe duly.
(transitive, or, intransitive) To engage in joyful activity in appreciation of an event.
(transitive) To perform or participate in, as a sacrament or solemn rite; to perform with appropriate rites.
famous or widely praised
The formal performance of a solemn rite, such as Christian sacrament.
A social gathering for entertainment and fun; a party.
(uncountable, uncommon outside high registers) Fame, renown; the state of being famous or talked-about. [from 17th c.]
(countable) A person who has a high degree of recognition by the general population for his or her success or accomplishments; a famous person. [from 19th c.]

Of or relating to chemistry.

A noxious substance contained in some form of delivery system such as a shell or missile.
A short nightdress, or similar piece of lingerie.
A person who specializes in the science of chemistry, especially at a professional level.

(uncountable) The branch of natural science that deals with the composition and constitution of substances and the changes that they undergo as a consequence of alterations in the constitution of their molecules.

the production of carbohydrates and other compounds from simple compounds such as carbon dioxide, using the oxidation of chemical nutrients as a source of energy rather than sunlight; it is limited to certain bacteria and fungi

A box, now usually a large strong box with a secure convex lid.
(obsolete) A coffin.
The place in which public money is kept; a treasury.
A chest of drawers.
(anatomy) The portion of the human body from the base of the neck to the top of the abdomen; the homologous area in some other animals.
The front (anterior) surface of this portion of the torso.

A hit or blow made with one's chest.
The androgenic hair of the chest (anterior thorax).
A piece of furniture which has multiple parallel, horizontal drawers stacked one above the other, used mainly for the storage of clean clothes.

Having a pliable or springy texture when chewed.

A young bird.
A young chicken.
A small passerine bird (songbird) of the genus Parus or the family Paridae.
(uncountable) The meat from this bird eaten as food.
(archaic) The young of any bird; a chick.

a large spotted deer, of genus Axis, native to India and Sri Lanka

Holes or rifts often occur in a sheet of cirrocumulus. Abbreviated Cc.

(physical chemistry) A form of isomerism in which, in one isomer two atoms or groups are on the same side of the plane of a double bond or ring, whereas in the other isomer they are on opposite sides; these are cis- and trans- isomers, respectively.

(chess, uncountable) The active placement of the pieces, or the process of achieving it.
Any lifelong disability attributable to a mental or physical impairment, manifested during childhood or later in the human development age.

One who deviates from accepted beliefs or policies, especially from a prescribed form of Communism.

Skill in performing tasks, especially with the hands.
Skillful with one's hands.

Of or concerning the devil: devilish, satanic.
Extremely wicked or cruel.
Occurring over or changing with time.

A plan, drawing, sketch or outline to show how something works, or show the relationships between the parts of a whole.
A graph or chart.

Any formal system of reasoning that arrives at a truth by the exchange of logical arguments.
Of or pertaining to dialectic; (in, _, philosophy) logically reasoned through the exchange of opposing ideas.
(philosophy) The concept of reality in which material things are in the constant process of change brought about by the tension between conflicting or interacting forces, elements, or ideas.
A person who studies regional differences in speech sounds.
The study of dialects.

[ca. 1480]

Tact and subtle skill in dealing with people so as to avoid or settle hostility.

A difficult position.

The removal of ambiguity.

The sound of swallowing, sometimes indicating fear.
(often, in the plural) The flesh around the teeth.

An edible substance taken from one of two species of sub-Saharan acacia trees, Senegalia senegal and Vachellia seyal, used in the food industry as a stabilizer (e.g. in soda, gumdrops and marshmallows) and other purposes including pharmaceuticals, paints and polishes.
A sugary, gelatinous material used to make candies.
A confectionery made of gelatin in the miniature shape of a toy bear
A very portable, short firearm, for hand use, which fires bullets or projectiles, such as a handgun, revolver, pistol, or Derringer.
(military) A cannon with relatively long barrel, operating with relatively low angle of fire, and having a high muzzle velocity.
A metal or wooden frame on which a piece of ordnance is mounted for firing or transportation.
Any of various breeds of dog used by hunters to find, flush out and retrieve birds and other game; an individual of such a breed.
(nautical) Any of the various types of small armed vessels.
Shots from a gun or guns, typically creating loud report.
A criminal armed with a gun, especially a professional killer.
An alloy of 88% copper, 10% tin and 2% zinc, originally used for making guns.
(military rank) An artillery soldier, especially one who holds private rank.
A person who operates a gun.
A location in the front of the muzzle of a gun.
An explosive mixture of saltpetre (potassium nitrate), charcoal and sulfur; formerly used in gunnery but now mostly used in fireworks.
(countable) The act of discharging a firearm.
The distance to which shot can be thrown from a gun; the reach or range of a gun.
An optical instrument which establishes an optical line or axis for the purpose of aiming a weapon.
A person skilled in the repair and servicing of firearms.
The top edge of the hull of a nautical vessel, where it meets the deck.
A plucked zither-like stringed instrument (chordophone), traditionally featuring seven unfretted strings, originating in ancient China.
(US) A stretcher having wheeled legs.
In Indian traditions: a spiritual teacher who transmits knowledge to a shishya. [from 17th c.]
A sudden rapid outflow.
(intransitive, also, figurative) To flow forth suddenly, in great volume.

(musical instrument) A plucked psaltery-like string instrument, usually played on the lap and sometimes created with table legs so that the musician can play it seated next to the instrument, originating in ancient Russian music.
A small piece of cloth inserted in a garment, for the purpose of strengthening some part or giving it a tapering enlargement cf. godet.
The ability to taste flavors; the sense of taste.
(idiomatic) An instinct or intuition; an immediate or basic feeling or reaction without a logical rationale.
(by extension, informal) Courage; determination.
An inelastic natural latex, produced from the sap of several tropical trees of the genera Palaquium and Payena.
A ditch along the side of a road.
(bowling) A groove down the sides of a bowling lane.
(especially, in the plural, often, controversial) A person (see usage notes).
(informal, term of address) Buster, Mack, fella, bud, man.
A zither-like stringed instrument with at least eighteen strings and moveable bridges, played with a plectrum, originating in the traditional music of China.
To drink or eat quickly, voraciously, or to excess; to gulp down; to swallow greedily, continually, or with gusto.
(especially, weightlifting) A sports facility specialized for lifting weights, cardio machines, and other exercise (culturally differentiated from sense 1).
(formal) A large room or building for indoor sports.
One who performs (the sport of) gymnastics.
A sport involving the performance of sequences of movements requiring physical strength, flexibility, and kinesthetic awareness.
(botany) Any plant such as a conifer whose seeds are not enclosed in an ovary.
(Commonwealth) .
(American spelling) The study of, or the branch of medicine specializing in, the medical problems of women, especially disorders of the reproductive organs.
(diseases) Excessive development of breasts in men, resembling the breast development in women.
Fear of or aversion to women or girls.
A Japanese crescent-shaped dumpling filled with a minced stuffing and steamed, boiled or fried; the Japanese equivalent of the Chinese jiaozi.
A mineral consisting of hydrated calcium sulphate. When calcinated, it forms plaster of Paris.
(colloquial) An itinerant person or any person, not necessarily Romani; a tinker, a traveller or a carny.
Falco rusticolus, a large bird of prey that breeds on Arctic coasts and islands of North America, Europe and Asia.
A style of Greek sandwich commonly filled with grilled meat, tomato, onions, and tzatziki sauce.

A polyhedral solid formed by joining two face-regular triangular prisms along corresponding square faces, giving a quarter-turn to one prism. It is noted for being one of the few regular polyhedra that packs in three dimensions.
A north-seeking form of gyroscope used as a directional reference in navigation.

An apparatus composed of a wheel which spins inside of a frame (gimbal) and causes the balancing of the frame in any direction or position. In the form of a gyroscopic stabilizer, used to help keep aircraft and ships steady.
(anatomy) A fold or ridge on the cerebral cortex of the brain.
(geometry) A convex shape which, if made of a uniformly dense material, has one stable equilibrium orientation and one unstable equilibrium orientation.
A representation of laughter.
(legal) A writ ordering that a person be brought before a court or a judge, most frequently used to ensure that a person's imprisonment, detention, or commitment is legal.
Ribbons, buttons, thread, needles and similar sewing goods sold in a haberdasher's shop.
A shop selling such goods.
An action performed on a regular basis.
An action performed repeatedly and automatically, usually without awareness.
An addiction.
A place in which a person lives.
One who frequents a place. [from 1818]
A violent duststorm or sandstorm in the deserts of Arabia, North Africa, India, or North America. [from late 19th c.]
Fruit of these plants.
(computer security, telecommunications) One who uses a computer to gain unauthorized access to data stored in, or to carry out malicious attacks on, computer networks or computer systems.
(transitive) To make uninteresting or trite by frequent use.
Repeated too often.
A saw, with a blade that is put under tension, for cutting metal
A marine fish, Melanogrammus aeglefinus, of the North Atlantic, important as a food fish.
(countable, religion, Islam) An eyewitness account of a saying or action of Muhammad or sometimes one of his companions not otherwise found in the Quran.
(particle) A composite particle that comprises two or more quarks held together by the strong force and (consequently) can interact with other particles via said force; a meson or a baryon.
(medicine) The scientific study of blood and blood-producing organs.
(Commonwealth, pathology) Any of several hereditary illnesses that impair the body's ability to control bleeding, usually passed from mother to son.
(chiefly, British, pathology) viral haemorrhagic fever
A pathological condition caused by painful masses of dilated veins in swollen anal tissue.
A chemical element (symbol Hf) with an atomic number of 72: a lustrous, silvery-grey tetravalent transition metal.
A witch, sorceress, or enchantress; a female wizard.
(pejorative) An ugly old woman.
Any of several primitive eellike fish, of the family Myxinidae, having a sucking mouth with rasping teeth, and sometimes used as food or for eelskin leather.
Looking exhausted, worried, or poor in condition

A traditional Scottish dish made from minced sheep offal with oatmeal and spices, etc., originally boiled in the stomach of a sheep but now often in an artificial casing, and usually served with neeps and tatties (mashed swede and potatoes) and accompanied with whisky.
A Japanese poem in three lines, the first and last consisting of five morae, and the second consisting of seven morae, usually with an emphasis on the season or a naturalistic theme.
(poetry) A person who writes haiku; a haiku poet.
(archaic, or, poetic) An exclamation of respectful or reverent salutation, or, occasionally, of familiar greeting.
(impersonal) To have hailstones fall from the sky.
A single ball of hail, or solid precipitation
(countable) A pigmented filament of keratin which grows from a follicle on the skin of humans and other mammals.
(uncountable) The collection or mass of such growths growing from the skin of humans and animals, and forming a covering for a part of the head or for any part or the whole body.
(cosmetics) A type of shampoo product that aims to improve the condition of the hair, especially after washing.
Any of various materials used to dye hair on the head.
A length of hair which is attached to one's normal hair to make it longer.
A tool that uses heat to curl, straighten, or crimp a person's head of hair.
(idiomatic) An alcoholic drink, particularly when taken the morning after to cure a hangover.
A small tube that is rolled into a person's hair in order to curl it, making a new hairstyle.
The establishment of a beautician or barber.
A usually scented hairstyling product in aerosol form that stiffens the hair, so it stays in a certain hairstyle.
A circular piece of elastic used to hold hair in place.
A small wad of fur or mass of hair formed in the digestive system of a cat or other animal, from hair ingested while grooming.
A brush used in hair care for brushing, tidying, and detangling hair
The act of cutting of the hair, often done professionally by a barber, hair stylist, or beautician.
A person who cuts or styles hair as an occupation or profession.
(chiefly, _, UK) A small electrical appliance for drying hair, by generating a stream of hot air.
Destitute of hair.
A net designed to keep hair up and out of the way, e.g. while cooking.
A pin or fastener for the hair.
The style in which someone's hair has been cut and arranged.
(of a person) Having a lot of body hair.
(Islam) The pilgrimage to Mecca made by pious Muslims; the fifth of the five pillars of Islam.
(Islam) a honorific given to Muslim who has participated in a hajj.

A group dance of New Zealand's Maori people featuring rhythmic chanting, vigorous facial and arm movements, and foot stamping. Traditionally a war dance, today it is also performed to welcome guests, as a mark of respect at occasions such as commemorations and funerals, as a challenge to opposing teams at sports events, and for artistic purposes.
(Islam) Allowable, according to Muslim religious customs, to have or do.
(specifically, of food) Fit to eat according to Muslim religious customs.

A two-handed pole weapon, consisting of a long pole with an axe-like blade mounted on it (at a right angle like an axe, not on the tip like a spear), and (opposite the blade) typically a spike or hook.
Consisting of some indefinite portion resembling a half; approximately a half, whether more or less; partial; imperfect.
One of two usually roughly equal parts into which anything may be divided, or considered as divided.
(preceded by “a” or a number) The fraction obtained by dividing 1 by 2.
(uncountable, travel) A hotel rate that includes accommodation, breakfast and dinner, but no meal at lunchtime.
A male sibling sharing a single parent, as distinguished from a full brother or brother-german, from a step-brother, or from a brother-like figure such as a blood brother.
son of one's half brother or half sister
Thirty minutes past any hour.
(horse racing) Any of two or more horses having the same dam but different sires.
(horse racing) A female half sibling (same dam, different sires).
(dated, derogatory, offensive, ethnic slur) A person of mixed racial parentage or ancestry, especially one of mixed white and American Indian parentage (metis, métis, Metis, Métis; mestizo).
A period of fifty years, half of a century.
A period of time equal to thirty minutes, half an hour.
At intervals of a half-hour, every 30 minutes.
(nuclear physics) The time required for half the nuclei in a sample of an isotope to undergo radioactive decay.
(physical chemistry) In a chemical reaction, the time required for the concentration of a reactant to fall from a chosen value to half that value.
(medicine, pharmacology) The time it takes for a substance (drug, radioactive nuclide, or other) to lose half of its pharmacological, physiologic, or radiological activity.
The moon in its first or last quarter when only half the visible face is illuminated; a quarter moon.
Anything shaped like a crescent, especially the base of a fingernail.
With very few clothes on.
(sports) The interval between the two halves of a sports match.
A half-brother of one's parent.
A half brother-in-law of one's parent.
Describes a hairstyle where only a section of hair is tied up behind the head (half-up) while the rest of the hair hangs freely (half-down).
The period of time equal to half a year; normally referred to as 6 months, but a half-year is more exactly 182.5 days (without a leap day)
(fantasy) A fictional small humanoid creature featuring in fantasy fiction; a hobbit.
Half of the way between two points
(computing, typography) Of a text character, occupying the space of half of a fullwidth character, or one "normal" text column.
A large flatfish of the genus Hippoglossus, which sometimes leaves the ocean floor and swims vertically.
(especially) Such a salt with a single halogen atom.
(pathology) The condition of having stale or foul-smelling breath.
A corridor; a hallway.
A large meeting room.
A building providing student accommodation at a university.

(usually, capitalized, often, _, sports) A structure housing memorials to famous or illustrious individuals (especially ones of importance to some field), often containing a collection of memorabilia relating to them.
(usually capitalized) A collection of the worst, most hated, or poorest-quality entries in a particular subject, medium, field, etc.
An exclamation used in songs of praise or thanksgiving to God.
An official marking made by a trusted party, usually an assay office, on items made of precious metals.
A traditional cheese from Cyprus, made from goat's and/or sheep's milk.
(ambitransitive) To seem to perceive things (with one or more of one's senses) which are not really present; to have visions; to experience a hallucination.
A sensory perception of something that does not exist, often arising from disorder of the nervous system, as in delirium tremens.
A circular band of coloured light, visible around the sun or moon etc., caused by reflection and refraction of light by ice crystals in the atmosphere.
The metaphorical aura of glory, veneration or sentiment which surrounds an idealized entity.
(religion) nimbus, a luminous disc, often of gold, around or over the heads of saints, etc., in religious paintings.
(chemistry) Any element of group 17, i.e. fluorine, chlorine, bromine, iodine, astatine and tennessine.
(intransitive) To stop either temporarily or permanently.
(transitive) To bring to a stop.
(transitive) To cause to discontinue.
A bitless headpiece of rope or straps, placed on the head of animals such as cattle or horses to lead or tie them.
(less common) A halter top or halterneck top (a garment with such a strap).
In a halting or limping manner; full of pauses or hesitation.
A confection usually made from crushed sesame seeds and honey. It is a traditional dessert in South Asia, the Mediterranean and the Middle East.
(anatomy) The region back of the knee joint; the popliteal space; the hock.
(acting) An overacting or amateurish performer; an actor with an especially showy or exaggerated style.
(countable) A thigh and/or buttock of a hog slaughtered for meat; (occasionally) the corresponding cut from some other animal.
(uncountable) Meat from the thigh and/or buttock of a hog cured for food.
(Greek mythology) A wood-nymph who was physically a part of her tree; she would die if her tree were felled.
The patty used in such a sandwich.
A small village or a group of houses.
(British) A village that does not have its own church.
Any of the fish of the genus Hypoplectrus in the family Serranidae.
A tool with a heavy head and a handle used for pounding.
(anatomy) The malleus, a small bone of the middle ear.
(sports) A device made of a heavy steel ball attached to a length of wire, and used for throwing.
A depiction of a sickle crossed with a hammer, used as a symbol of communism and the Soviet Union.
An athletic throwing event where the object to be thrown is a heavy steel ball attached with wire (maximum length 4 ft (1.22 m)) to a handle.
(athletics) An athlete who competes in the hammer throw.
Any of various sharks of the genus Sphyrna having the eyes set on projections (cephalofoils) from the sides of the head, which gives it a hammer shape.
A swinging couch or bed, usually made of netting or canvas about six feet (1.8 meters) wide, suspended by clews or cords at the ends.

In particular, a rodent of the species Mesocricetus auratus (the golden hamster) or of a species of the genera Cricetiscus and Phodopus (the dwarf hamsters), often kept as a pet or used in scientific research.
(anatomy) One of the great tendons situated in each side of the ham, or space back of the knee, and connected with the muscles of the back of the thigh.

A sign used in the written Arabic language representing a glottal stop. Hamza may appear as a stand-alone letter (ء‎) or most commonly diacritically over or under other letters, e.g. أ‎ (over an alif [ا‎]), إ‎ (under an alif), ؤ‎ (over a wāw [و‎]) or ئ‎ (over a dotless yāʾ [ى‎]). The exact seat of hamza is governed by an orthographic rule – the "seat of hamza rule".
Sorrowful resentment, as a part of the Korean cultural identity.
The Japanese custom of enjoying the beauty of flowers, usually cherry blossoms or plum blossoms, also known as "flower viewing".
The traditional Korean dress, often characterized by vibrant colours and simple lines without pockets.
The part of the forelimb below the forearm or wrist in a human, and the corresponding part in many other animals.
A limb of certain animals, such as the foot of a hawk, or any one of the four extremities of a monkey.
That which is, or may be, held in a hand at once.
(card games) The set of cards held by a player.
(chiefly, in measuring the height of horses) Four inches, a hand's breadth.
A side; part, camp; direction, either right or left.
Power of performance; means of execution; ability; skill; dexterity.
Applause.
An electric-powered device in a restroom to dry hands with a stream of warm air.
A hand-held device designed to be waved back and forth in order to induce airflow for the purpose of cooling the user.
(military) A small hand-held explosive device designed to be thrown at an enemy.
Holding or clasping hands.
(vulgar, slang) The stimulation of another person's penis using the hand as a sexual act.
(transitive) To distribute; to give out, either by hand or as if so (figuratively). [from 17th c.]
(transitive, idiomatic) To relinquish control or possession of something to someone.
A puppet operated by the hand, especially one in which the puppeteer's hand occupies and controls the head.
(mineral) A disinfecting liquid, most often based on ethyl alcohol, used as an alternative to washing the hands with soap and water.
A tool powered by human muscular action rather than a motor or engine.

cit.quote: 手と目のコーディネーション

sense.def: The degree of coordination a person has between their eyes and their hands; a person's dexterity in activities highly dependent upon sight, such as catching a ball.
Held in one or both hands.
Small and light enough to be operated while held in one or both hands.
(especially) A piece of clothing or other item which has been outgrown by an older sibling and passed down to a younger one.
A semi-voiced diacritic (゜) used with Japanese kana to change a /h/ to a /p/.
(now, rare) A small bag carried in the hand, used either when travelling or to carry tools for a specific job. [from 19th c.]
(uncountable) A team sport where two teams of seven players each (six players and a goalkeeper) pass and bounce a ball trying to throw it in the goal of the opposing team.
(countable, Australian rules football) An act of passing a football by holding it with one hand and hitting it with the other.
A person who plays handball, especially professionally.
(music) A small bell designed to be rung by hand.
A topically organized book of reference on a certain field of knowledge, regardless of size, but archetypally one to be kept readily at hand.

(mechanical engineering, automotive, railroading) The mechanism, particularly the locking hand-operated lever or foot-operated toggle lever in a motorcar or the hand-operated crank on a railcar, which is used to set and release such a brake.
A cart designed to be pulled or pushed by hand (as opposed to with a beast of burden.)
A fastening consisting of two metal rings, designed to go around a person's wrists, and connected by a chain or hinge.
The amount that a hand will grasp or contain.
A small number, usually approximately five.

(sports) An allowance of a certain amount of time or distance in starting, granted in a race (or other contest of skill) to the competitor possessing disadvantages; or an additional weight or other hindrance imposed upon the one possessing advantages, in order to equalize, as much as possible, the chances of success.
(sometimes considered offensive) The disadvantage itself, in particular physical or mental disadvantages of people.
(sometimes considered, _, offensive) Having a handicap.
A trade requiring skill of hand; manual occupation; handcraft.
An artifact produced by handicraft.
A piece of cloth, usually square and often fine and elegant, carried for wiping the face, eyes, nose or hands.
The part of an object which is (designed to be) held in the hand when used or moved.
(mostly, in the plural) The bar used to steer a bicycle, motorbike, or similar vehicle using the hands.
A touching, controlling, managing, using, taking care of, etc., with the hand or hands, or as with the hands.
A handheld mirror
A printed sheet such as a leaflet or pamphlet, or a worksheet, that is given out free of charge (usually by hand) for a certain use, for example as an advertisement or for information.
(informal, often, derogatory) A gift of money or material assistance to the needy or poor.
Tending not to interfere with the decisions and actions of other people (employees, subjects, etc.).
(informal) Refrain from touching; refrain from initiating any physical contact.
(idiomatic) Surrender (by raising your hands)!
A saw small enough to be used by one hand.
The part of a landline telephone containing both receiver and transmitter (and sometimes dial), held in the hand.
The grasping of hands by two people when greeting, leave-taking, or making an agreement.
(computing) An exchange of signals between two devices when communications begin in order to ensure synchronization.
Of a man or boy: attractively manly, having a pleasing face and overall effect.
A somersault made with the assistance of the hands placed upon the ground.
The washing of one's hands.
The characteristic writing of a particular person.
Easy to use, useful.
Nearby, within reach.
Dexterous, skilful. (of a person)
(informal) A person who does small tasks and odd jobs, especially building repairs and the like.
(fashion) traditional Han Chinese clothing
(intransitive) To be or remain suspended.
(transitive) To hold or bear in a suspended or inclined manner or position instead of erect.
(intransitive, informal) To loiter; to hang around; to spend time idly.
(transitive, chess) To cause (a piece) to become vulnerable to capture.
An unpowered aircraft resembling a large kite from which a rider is suspended in a harness.
The sport of flying in a hang glider.
(mostly, imperative) To wait a moment.
To persevere.
(dated, informal) To be unyielding; to hold out.
(transitive) To put up to hang.
(intransitive, idiomatic) To terminate a telephone call, originally by hanging the receiver on its hook or cradle thereby automatically disconnecting the line.
A large garage-like structure where aircraft are kept.
One who hangs, or causes to be hanged; a hangman, paper hanger, etc.
Someone who hangs on, or sticks to, a person, place, or service.
(countable, uncountable) The act of hanging a person (or oneself) by the neck in order to kill that person (or to commit suicide).
(countable) Anything that is hung as a decorative element (such as curtains, gobelins, or posters).
(countable) An executioner responsible for hanging criminals.
A loose, narrow strip of nail tissue protruding from the side edge and anchored near the base of a fingernail or toenail.
Negative effects, such as headache or nausea, caused by previous drunkenness due to (excessive) consumption of alcohol.
(figurative) An unpleasant relic left from prior events.
The phonetic alphabet used to write the Korean language.
(genetics) A group of closely related haplotypes.
(genetics, strictly) Having a single set of unpaired chromosomes (which is the number that a typical gamete has in many organisms although not all).
(phonology, uncountable) The process of deleting one of two almost identical syllables within a word.
(transitive, archaic) To happen to; to befall.
(slang, of a person or product) Trendy, up-to-the-minute.
In a happy or cheerful manner; with happiness.
By good chance; fortunately, successfully.
With good will; in all happiness; willingly.

(idiomatic) Chiefly preceded by he, she, they, etc., lived: often used as a formulaic ending in fairy tales, stories for children, and similar works: in a state of happiness for the rest of his, her, their, etc., lives.
(uncountable) The emotion of being happy; joy; elation.
(archaic, uncountable) Good luck; good fortune.
Having a feeling arising from a consciousness of well-being or of enjoyment; enjoying good of any kind, such as comfort, peace, or tranquillity; blissful, contented, joyous.
Experiencing the effect of favourable fortune; favored by fortune or luck; fortunate, lucky, propitious.
An expression used during Easter to wish someone a happy time.

cit.quote: 明けましておめでとうございます
良いお年をお迎え下さい
明けましておめでとう

sense.def: A wish said around the start of a new year to wish someone well for the New Year (holiday) or for the (entire) new year.

cit.quote: ハッピーバレンタイン
お誕生日おめでとうございます

sense.def: Said or written to a person who is celebrating their birthday in order to convey the good wishes of the speaker or writer (literally, "may you have a happy birthday")

cit.quote: ハッピーエンディング

sense.def: (narratology) A conclusion to a story in which all the loose ends of the plot are tied up, and all the main characters are left in a state of contentment or happiness.

(North America, Philippines) A greeting used during the Christmas and winter holiday season to recognize the celebration of many holidays, sometimes starting with Thanksgiving and including Hanukkah, the winter solstice, Christmas, Kwanzaa, and New Year's Day.
(chemistry) A measure of the number of atoms of a ligand that are coordinated to a central atom.
(microbiology) A kind of unicellular marine phytoplankton, typically covered in tiny scales or plates composed of carbohydrates and calcium deposits
A type of traditional Cantonese shrimp dumpling; the outer skin is translucent and the filling is made of shrimp.
Ceremonial suicide by disembowelment, as by slicing open the abdomen with a dagger or knife: formerly practised in Japan by the samurai when disgraced or sentenced to death.
Suicide or any suicidal action.
(linguistics) Diacritics marking short vowels in Arabic script.
(Islam, fiqh) Forbidden by Islam: unlawful, sinful.
Persistent attacks and criticism causing worry and distress.
A person or thing that foreshadows or foretells the coming of someone or something.
(countable, nautical) A sheltered expanse of water, adjacent to land, in which ships may anchor or dock, especially for loading and unloading.
(of drink or drugs) Strong.
Resistant to pressure; difficult to break, cut, or penetrate.
Difficult or requiring a lot of effort to do, understand, experience, or deal with.
(manner) With much force or effort.
(US) An alcoholic beverage formed by fermenting cider (apple juice).
(computer hardware) One of a series of parallel magnetic recording disks in a drive unit, used for the recording and retrieval of digital information; used especially in personal computers.
(computer hardware) The unit itself, and all the disks within it.

(computing, computer hardware) An electromechanical data storage device that stores and retrieves digital data using magnetic storage with one or more rigid, rapidly rotating platters coated with magnetic material.
A helmet, usually made from rigid plastic, used on construction sites to protect the head from falling objects.
A thin horizontal bony plate of the skull, located in the roof of the mouth.
(music genre) A rock music genre marked by a heavy regular beat, high amplification, and usually frenzied performances.
(chemistry) Water with a high concentration of dissolved minerals, especially calcium, making it difficult to lather with soap.
Cooked to a solid consistency. (of a boiled egg)
Callous and unsentimental. (of a person, especially a detective)
A person who takes a firm and uncompromising position on some policy.
(slang, vulgar) An erection of the penis.
(idiomatic, usually reflexive, dated) To make someone more resistant to something.
Stubborn; wilful.
(music genre) A genre of electronic dance music that combines elements of trance, techno, and hardcore, with origins in the Netherlands and Belgium.
(nautical) A large, hard biscuit made from unleavened flour and water; formerly used as a long-term staple food aboard ships.
(computing) The part of a computer that is fixed and cannot be altered without replacement or physical modification; motherboard, expansion cards, etc. Compare software.
A shop that sells tools, fasteners, and similar objects known collectively as hardware, as well as related sundries used in construction and repair.
Of a person, taking their work seriously and doing it well and rapidly.
Having rugged physical strength; inured to fatigue or hardships.
(uncountable) The meat from this animal.
(teratology) A congenital malformation of the upper lip, reminiscent of the mouth of a hare.
The private section of a Muslim household forbidden to male strangers. [from 1841]
A pantomime fool, typically dressed in colorful checkered clothes, used as a stock character in commedia dell'arte and other genres.
A North American wild duck, Histrionicus histrionicus.
Physical injury; hurt; damage.
To damage, hurt, or injure something, usually an inanimate object.
Causing or likely to cause harm or damage; injurious.
The characteristic of being harmful.
Incapable of causing harm or danger; safe.
The characteristic of being harmless.

(analysis) A study of the representation of functions or signals as the superposition of basic waves, involving the notions of harmonic functions, trigonometric series, Fourier series, Fourier transforms, almost periodic functions, and others.
(mathematics) A function of two, three or n variables which is a solution to any of Laplace's equations
(mathematics) A type of measure of central tendency calculated as the reciprocal of the mean of the reciprocals, i.e., H = { n \over {1 \over x_1} + {1 \over x_2} + \cdots + {1 \over x_n} }.
(number theory) Any of a series of numbers formed from the sum of the reciprocals of consecutive natural numbers

(uncountable, figurative) an area or place where one feels familiar or at home.
(Internet) The main or first page of a website or set of hyperlinked documents.

(baseball) A flat, pentagonal, rubber object placed at the center of the batter's box, which is used as a basis for judging pitched strikes and balls, and the touching of which by a runner advancing from or past third base scores a run.

(pesäpallo) A three-base hit, a legal hit where the batter gets to third base without stopping and without the opposing team attempting to put the batter out on earlier bases, scoring one run immediately.
(figurative, by extension) The final part of a distance or the final effort needed to finish.
