sense.def: (idiomatic) One's home, especially a nice, comfortable home.
(slang, derogatory) A person who gains the affections of someone already married or engaged, and thus causes the dissolution of the marriage or engagement.
(North American, informal) A person who prefers to remain at home, rather than participate in social events elsewhere.

Ellipsis of harvest homecoming, a traditional (street) party and/or dance near the start of the school year, at around fall mid-terms. It traditionally marks the start of harvest break, where students go home in autumn to harvest the crops on the family farms.
The country that one regards as home.
Lacking a permanent place of residence.
The state of being homeless.
(pseudoscience) A system of treating diseases with small amounts of substances which, in larger amounts, would produce the observed symptoms.

(physiology) The ability of a system or living organism to adjust its internal environment to maintain a state of dynamic constancy; such as the ability of warm-blooded animals to maintain a stable temperature.
Someone who owns a house.
(often with for) Missing one's home and family very much when away; nostalgic.
The characteristic of being homesick; a strong, sad feeling of missing one's home (and often left-behind loved ones, such as family and friends) when physically away.
An individual’s place of birth, childhood home, or place of main residence.
Towards home.
Leading toward home.
(literally, now, _, rare) Any work that is done at home; housework.
(countable, uncountable, crime) The killing of one person by another, whether premeditated or unintentional.
(countable) A person who kills another.
A variety of domesticated rock pigeon (Columba livia) that has been selectively bred to be able to find its way home over extremely long distances.
(colloquial, often, pejorative) Clipping of homosexual.
(dated, US, Canada) Homogenized milk with a high butterfat content.
The condition of being homogeneous: having uniformity of constituent content.

(ring theory, of an element of a graded ring) Belonging to one of the summands of the grading (if the ring is graded over the natural numbers and the element is in the kth summand, it is said to be homogeneous of degree k; if the ring is graded over a commutative monoid I, and the element is an element of the ith summand, it is said to be of grade i)
A word that is spelled the same as another word, usually having a different etymology.
(broadly) A word that sounds or is spelled the same as another word (but not necessarily both).
Hatred, fear, dislike of, or prejudice against homosexuals, or LGBTQ people in general. [from 1971]
(semantics) A word which is pronounced the same as another word but differs in spelling or meaning or origin.
(statistics) A property of a set of random variables such that each variable has the same finite variance.

(of a person or other animal, formal, distancing, or, dated) Sexually and/or romantically attracted to members of the same sex, such as a man who is attracted to men or a woman who is attracted to women; gay. (Typically used in the sense of sole/exclusive attraction.)
(of a romantic or sexual act or relationship, formal, distancing, or, dated) Between two people of the same sex; gay.
(typically, formal, distancing, or, dated) A person who is sexually attracted solely or primarily to others of the same sex.
Sexual activity with a person of the same sex, sometimes (potentially, _, offensive) restricted to same-sex sex between males. [1897]
(topology) A continuous deformation of one continuous function or map to another.
A miniature man, once imagined by spermists to be present in human sperm.
A sharpening stone composed of extra-fine grit used for removing the burr or curl from the blade of a razor or some other edge tool.
(transitive) To sharpen with a hone; to whet.
(of a person or institution) Scrupulous with regard to telling the truth; not given to swindling, lying, or fraud; upright.
(manner) In an honest manner.
(sentence adverb) Frankly, to be honest.
Used to express exasperation, dismay, etc.
(uncountable, countable) The act, quality, or condition of being honest.

cit.quote: 正直は最高の政策です

sense.def: (uncountable) A sweet, viscous, gold-colored fluid produced from plant nectar by bees, and often consumed by humans.
A spectrum of pale yellow to brownish-yellow color, like that of most types of (the sweet substance) honey.
A term of affection.
Mellivora capensis, a badger-like mustelid native to Africa, the Middle East and the Indian subcontinent.
Any of seven species of bee, in genus Apis, often kept commercially for honey, beeswax, and pollination of crops.
A turned kitchen tool used to transfer honey.
A parasitic mushroom of the genus Armillaria that lives on trees and shrubs.
(idiomatic) The use of a romantic or a sexual relationship to entice a person into revealing secret information.

(uncountable) A substance made by bees (clade Anthophila) primarily from beeswax which has hexagonal cells to hold their larvae, and for storing pollen and honey to feed the larvae and themselves when other food is scarce; it is also eaten by humans as part of comb-honey; (countable) a single sheet made up of two layers of this substance.
(countable, by extension) Something resembling honeycomb (sense 1) in having numerous cells or small holes.
(uncountable) A sweet, sticky substance deposited on leaves and other plant parts by insects (especially aphids and scale insects) feeding on plant sap, or by fungi.
Any of the many Australasian birds of the family Meliphagidae, which have a tongue adapted for obtaining nectar from flowers.
Any of several brood-parasitic Old World tropical birds, of the family Indicatoridae, that primarily feed on wax, especially beeswax.
The period of time immediately following a marriage.
A trip taken by a newly married couple during this period.
Synonym of red envelope.
(transitive, intransitive) To use a car horn.
(intransitive) To make a loud, harsh sound like a car horn.
(uncountable) Recognition of importance or value; respect; veneration (of someone, usually for being morally upright or successful).
(countable) A token of praise or respect; something that represents praiseworthiness or respect, such as a prize or award given by the state to a citizen.
(transitive) To think of highly, to respect highly; to show respect for; to recognise the importance or spiritual value of.
(US) A student enrolled in an honor society.
A term of respect; respectful language.

(euphemistic) A typically Middle Eastern and South Asian cultural practice whereby a family member, usually female, is murdered by other family members, the act being justified as retribution for a (usually sexual) slight upon the family's honour.
(British spelling) Respected, having received honour.
An underclassman or junior, in the context of Korea.
A covering for the head, usually attached to a larger garment such as a jacket or cloak.
Grus monacha, a bird of the crane (Gruidae) family, native to East Asia
A grey and black Eurasian crow, Corvus cornix.
A sweatshirt with an integral hood and, sometimes, a large kangaroo pocket at the front.
A rough or violent youth.
(geology) A tall thin spire of rock that protrudes from the bottom of arid basins and badlands.
The tip of a toe of an ungulate such as a horse, ox or deer, strengthened by a thick keratin covering.
A rod bent into a curved shape, typically with one end free and the other end secured to a rope or other attachment.
(music) A catchy musical phrase which forms the basis of a popular song.
(boxing) a type of punch delivered with the arm rigid and partially bent and the fist travelling nearly horizontally mesially along an arc

(basketball) a basketball shot in which the offensive player, usually turned perpendicular to the basket, gently throws the ball with a sweeping motion of his arm in an upward arc with a follow-through which ends over his head. Also called hook shot.
(transitive) To assemble the parts of a mechanism, especially by connecting wires.
(recreational inhalants) A pipe with a long flexible tube that draws the smoke through water, traditionally used for smoking tobacco, which is often flavored.
(informal, attributive) A young person who causes trouble or violence, typically as a member of a gang or other group.
unruly, aggressive behavior; behavior associated with hooligans
A circular band of metal used to bind a barrel.
Any Old World bird of genus Upupa, especially Upupa epops (Eurasian hoopoe), known for its distinctive plumage, fanlike crest, and slender bill.
Used to express approval, joy or victory.
To cry out or shout in contempt.
The horn in a motor vehicle.
(usually, in the plural) The flowers of the hop plant, dried and used to brew beer etc.
(US, slang) Opium, or some other narcotic drug.
(intransitive) To jump a short distance.
A Ukrainian national dance in 2/4 time.
(countable, _, or, _, uncountable) The feeling of trust, confidence, belief or expectation that something wished for can or will happen.
(countable) A person or thing that is a source of hope.
To want (something) to happen, with a sense of expectation that it might [with that (+ clause); or (informal) with clause; or with so or (negative) not].
(uncomparable) It is hoped that; I hope; we hope. [from 18th c.]
Giving no ground of hope; promising nothing desirable; desperate.
A lack of hope; despair.

A sweet beverage variously made with rice, chufa or morro seeds (or, historically, barley), water, sugar, and cinnamon, and sometimes with milk.
A wandering troop or gang; especially, a clan or tribe of a nomadic people (originally Tatars) migrating from place to place for the sake of pasturage, plunder, etc.; a predatory multitude.
The visible horizontal line (in all directions) where the sky appears to meet the earth in the distance.
Perpendicular to the vertical; parallel to the plane of the horizon; level, flat.
(gymnastics) A horizontally-aligned bar used in gymnastics, upon which acts of swinging are performed.

(economics) The integrating of identical stages in the production or marketing process under the ownership or control of a single management organization, typically by mergers and acquisitions in the same industry, to increase market share, reduce competition, or achieve economies of scale.
(physiology) Any substance produced by one tissue and conveyed by the bloodstream to another to effect physiological activity.
(LGBTQ, colloquial, usually, in the plural) Sex hormones, as used in hormone replacement therapy for transgender or intersex people.
(pharmacology) A synthetic compound with the same activity.

Any similar real or imaginary growth or projection such as the elongated tusk of a narwhal, the eyestalk of a snail, the pointed growth on the nose of a rhinoceros, or the hornlike projection on the head of a demon or similar.
(uncountable) The hard substance from which animals' horns are made, sometimes used by man as a material for making various objects.
An object whose shape resembles a horn, such as cornucopia or the point of an anvil.
(countable, musical instrument) An instrument resembling a musical horn and used to signal others.
(countable, automotive) A loud alarm, especially one on a motor vehicle.
A tree of the genus Carpinus, having a smooth gray bark and a ridged trunk, the wood being white and very hard, common along the banks of streams in the United States.
Any of various birds of the family Bucerotidae, with bills resembling a cow's horns. Many species have a casque above the bill, and many imprison their young in a tree.
(US, slang) A person (particularly a man) who is fixated on sex.
(US) A lark, Eremophila alpestris, with distinctive facial markings.
A plant of the species Cucumis metulifer, bearing a cucumber-like fruit.
An owl of the genus Bubo native to the Americas, among the largest types of owl, having two horn-like tufts of feathers on its head.

A large wasp, of the genus Vespa, having a brown-and-yellow-striped body and the ability to inflict a serious sting.

An astrological forecast of a person's future based on such information.
Causing horror; terrible; shocking.
(countable, uncountable) An intense distressing emotion of fear or repugnance.
(countable) An individual work in this genre.
(uncountable) A genre of fiction designed to evoke a feeling of fear and suspense.
(mostly, North America) A motion picture which entertains by horrifying or frightening the audience.

sense.def: (food) A small, light, and usually savory first course in a meal.
(by extension) Anything of secondary concern; not the primary thing.
(dated, rare) Something unusual or extraordinary.
Any member of the species Equus ferus, including the Przewalski's horse and the extinct Equus ferus ferus.
Any of a group of flies, Gasterophilinae, that are parasitic to equines.
A competitive race for horses carrying jockeys; often the subject of betting
A sport where horses and their jockeys compete to race around a track the fastest.
A posture in Asian martial arts which takes its name from the position assumed when riding a horse.
A type of sucking worm, Haemopis sanguisuga, larger than the common leech.
On the back of a horse.
(usually with on, upon, etc.) The back of a horse.
Any of several medium to large flies, of the family Tabanidae, that suck the blood of mammals (not to be confused with Stomoxys calcitrans, the stable fly, or dog fly).
The hair of a horse, especially from the mane and tail, used for upholstery.
A man who rides a horse.
The meat from a horse.
Metric horsepower, a metric unit approximately equal to 735.5 watts.
(countable) A plant of the mustard family, Armoracia rusticana, cultivated for its edible root.
(uncountable) A pungent condiment made from the root of the plant.
The practice of riding horses for sport or pleasure; equestrianism
(chiefly, Britain, idiomatic) Different people are suited for different jobs or situations; what is fitting in one case may not be fitting in another.
The U-shaped shoe of a horse, now typically made of metal; by extension, a representation of this used to play the game horseshoes, hung as a luck charm, etc.
(especially) Any extant xiphosuran in the family Limulidae.
Any extinct or extant chelicerate in the order Xiphosura, actually more related to arachnids than true crabs.

A pine tree, Pinus massoniana, native to a wide area of central and southern China, including Hong Kong and Taiwan, and northern Vietnam.
(childish, or, endearing) A child's term or name for a horse.
The art or science of cultivating gardens; gardening.

A cry of praise or adoration to God in liturgical use among the Jews, and said to have been shouted in recognition of the Messiahship of Jesus on his entry into Jerusalem; hence since used in the Christian Church.
(countable) A flexible tube conveying water or other fluid.

(uncountable) The provision of palliative care for terminally ill patients, either at a specialized facility or at a residence, and support for the family, typically refraining from taking extraordinary measures to prolong life.
cordial and generous towards guests
A large medical facility, usually in a building with multiple floors, where seriously ill or injured patients are given extensive medical or surgical treatment.
The act or service of welcoming, receiving, hosting, or entertaining guests; an appropriate attitude of openness, respect, and generosity toward guests.
(business) The business of providing catering, lodging and entertainment service; the industry which includes the operation of hotels, restaurants, and similar enterprises.
The hospitalizing of a patient, the condition of being hospitalized, or the period a patient stays in hospital.
To send to hospital; to admit (a person) to hospital.
Lying in a hospital, having been hospitalized.
One which receives or entertains a guest, socially, commercially, or officially.
A person or organization responsible for running an event.
(computing, Internet) Any computer attached to a network.
A country in which an international event is held.
A country which is the target of immigration.

A person given as a pledge or security for the performance of the conditions of a treaty or similar agreement, such as to ensure the status of a vassal.
A commercial overnight lodging place, with dormitory accommodation and shared facilities, especially a youth hostel.

sense.def: A bar hostess or bargirl; a paid female companion offering conversation and in some cases sex.
Not friendly; appropriate to an enemy; showing the disposition of an enemy; showing ill will and malevolence or a desire to thwart and injure.
Aggressive; antagonistic.
An attempted takeover of a company that is strongly resisted by the target company's management.
(uncountable) The state of being hostile.
(countable) A hostile action, especially a military action. See hostilities for specific plural definition.
(computing) Running and maintaining a computer system on someone's behalf.
(of a person or animal) Feeling the sensation of heat, especially to the point of discomfort.
(colloquial, of a person) Very physically or sexually attractive.
(of an object) Having or giving off a high temperature.
(of food) Spicy, pungent, piquant, as some chilis and other spices are.
Any one of several soups, served in various Asian cuisines, which are both spicy and sour
(countable) A serving of this beverage.
A sausage, typically a frankfurter.
A food item (dish) consisting of a frankfurter or wiener and (usually) a hot dog bun, with toppings such as ketchup, mustard, relish, sauerkraut, onions, cheese, etc.

A communal meal, popular in China, where diners share a bowl of hot broth or stock into which uncooked foods such as mushrooms, vegetables, and cuts of meat are dipped until they are cooked enough to be eaten.
Any liquid spicy condiment or cooking ingredient made from chili peppers.
(geology, planetology) The surface manifestation of a plume of molten material that rises from deep in a celestial body's mantle.
A natural spring producing water whose temperature is greater than about 20 °C (68 °F).
Used other than figuratively or idiomatically: see hot,‎ water.
A flexible, saclike bottle, usually made of rubber, intended to be filled with hot water and placed on some part of the body for thermotherapy, or simple warming.

An apparatus, usually fuel-burning, electric or solar-powered, in which water is heated to be used directly as domestic hot water or process hot water (but not for supplying space heating, calorifiers etc, for which a boiler or furnace is used).
A balloon-shaped aircraft whose bag is inflated with hot air, carrying passengers and crew in a gondola slung underneath.
(by extension) An environment that is ideal for the growth or development of something, especially of something undesirable.
An establishment that provides accommodation and other services for paying guests; normally larger than a guesthouse, and often one of a chain. [from 17th c.]
Someone who owns or runs a hotel.
A heated greenhouse.
(figuratively) A person who is very fragile and vulnerable as a result of having been sheltered.
A telephone line that is always staffed and able to give immediate assistance.
A direct line between two people, especially one between heads of state to be used in an emergency.
A semiportable stove.
A dog, particularly a breed with a good sense of smell developed for hunting other animals.
Fabric with a houndstooth pattern; an item of clothing made with such fabric.
(time) A unit of time of one twenty-fourth of a day (sixty minutes).
(Christianity, in the plural) The set times of prayer, the canonical hours, the offices or services prescribed for these, or a book containing them.

A clock made of two glass vessels connected by a narrow passage through which sand flows.
(Islam) A beautiful virgin girl supposed to dwell in Paradise for the enjoyment of the faithful.
A building used for something other than a residence (typically with qualifying word). [from 10th c.]
(politics) A building where a deliberative assembly meets; whence the assembly itself, particularly a component of a legislature. [from 10th c.]
(legal) Confinement of a person to his or her residence, sometimes with a limited travel allowance, ordered by a judge or other authority as a more lenient alternative to imprisonment.
Common house gecko (Hemidactylus frenatus), native to southeast Asia.
The universally common mouse of the species Mus musculus.

A structure made by stacking playing cards in a pyramidal fashion.
(figurative, idiomatic) A structure or argument built on a shaky foundation.
A bird of the species Passer domesticus, native to much of Eurasia, introduced in many other temperate environments.
Troglodytes aedon, a very small songbird of the wren family.
(chiefly, historical) A young male domestic servant, especially in a British colony in former times.
An old cloth or rag used to clean something, especially a house.
Any fly regularly found in human dwellings.
A machine which accomplishes a household function, such as cooking or cleaning.
A man who tends to his home as a housekeeper or homemaker; the male equivalent of a housewife.
Someone who manages the running of a home, traditionally the female head of the household. [from 17th c.]
The chores of maintaining a house as a residence, especially cleaning.
Someone living in the same house.
A woman in charge of a residence for young people to look after them.
(idiomatic) A party to celebrate moving into a new home.
(plural "housewives") The wife of a householder; the mistress of a family; the female head of a household.
domestic household chores such as cleaning and cooking
container

(mostly, science fiction) A levitating board that can be ridden in the manner of a surfboard or skateboard.
(vehicle, genericized trademark) A vehicle supported on a cushion of air, able to traverse many different types of terrain and travel over water, used for transport.
Any of various flies from the family Syrphidae that hover in the air and feed on the nectar of flowers.
(interrogative) To what degree or extent.
In any manner in which; in whatever way; however.
(exclamative) Used as a modifier to indicate surprise, delight, or other strong feelings in an exclamation.

(idiomatic, informal) Why; why is it; for what reason or purpose; due to what cause?
Used to express indignation and shock at another person's actions.

The protracted, mournful cry of a dog, wolf or other canid; also of other animals.
A prolonged cry of distress or anguish; a wail.

To utter a sound expressive of pain or distress; to cry aloud and mournfully; to lament; to wail.
The act of producing howls.
The currency of Ukraine, symbol ₴, divided into 100 kopiykas.
A class of Chinese alcoholic beverages made from fermented grains including rice, millet, and wheat, typically 10–20% alcohol by volume.

A confused uproar, commotion, tumult or racket.

A decorative and protective disk that covers the hub of a motor car wheel.
Excessive pride, presumption, or arrogance (originally toward the gods).
A color, or shade of color; tint; dye.

A close embrace, especially when charged with an emotion such as affection, joy, relief, lust, anger, aggression, compassion, and the like, as opposed to being characterized by formality, equivocation or ambivalence (a half-embrace or "little hug").

Very large.
the quality of being huge; immensity.

A hummed tune, i.e. created orally with lips closed.

Humanitarianism, philanthropy.
Relating to people's welfare.

(originally, US, idiomatic) A judicial or quasi-judicial proceeding, or a group of people which conducts such proceedings, which is without proper authority, and often acts abusively or decides unjustly. [from mid 19th c.]

An ornamental hairpin; hair ornament.
A sorghum-based variety of baijiu.

The tenth letter of the Greek alphabet.

(Hinduism, Buddhism, Sikhism, Jainism) The sum total of a person's actions, which determine the person's next incarnation in samsara, the cycle of death and rebirth.

Belief that multiple deities exist, and different deities are supreme among them at different times.

(Zen Buddhism): A word shouted out in Zen Buddhism (as well as other sects of Buddhism), and in East Asian martial arts schools, used to help focus the energy (気), and thereby induce an enlightened state.
One of two species of trees in the genus Cercidiphyllum, most commonly Cercidiphyllum japonicum, one of the largest trees in Asia.
A plant from the South Pacific, Piper methysticum.
An intoxicating beverage made from the kava plant.
(chiefly, in the context of Japanese culture, ACG) Cute, adorable.

(chiefly, in the context of Japanese culture) The quality of being kawaii; cuteness.

To observe the deceased overnight.
A person charged with guarding or caring for, storing, or maintaining something; a custodian, a guard; sometimes a gamekeeper.
A fermented milk drink from the Caucasus and Eastern Europe, similar to yogurt but more liquid.

Any of several large brown algae seaweeds (order Laminariales).
(Celtic mythology) A malevolent shapeshifting spirit, most often in the form of a horse, believed to haunt the rivers and lochs of Scotland.

A covering for the head, worn on solemn occasions by church dignitaries, which has been made in many forms, mostly recently a tall cap with two points or peaks.
A type of glove or garment that covers a hand with a separate sheath for the thumb, but not for other fingers, which are either enclosed in a single section or left uncovered.
(transitive) To combine (items from two or more sources normally kept separate).
Having two or more separate aspects.
Stemming from two or more races or breeds.
(sports) A game played between two teams, each consisting of a female and a male.
Marriage between people of different socially-distinguished groups, such as different races, cultures or religions.
(sports, martial arts) A style of combat sport allowing a wide range of combat techniques such as striking and grappling.
(math) A number consisting of a whole number and a fraction, such as 11½.
The state of diverse reception, when there are many who praise something while there are also many who dislike it.
One who, or a device that, mixes or merges things together.
A machine outfitted with (typically blunt) blades with which it mixes or beats ingredients in a bowl below.
Something (especially a series of ideas, letters, words, etc.) used to help in remembering a thing; a memory aid.
(plurale tantum) The study of techniques for remembering anything more easily.

Any of several species of large, extinct, flightless birds of the family Dinornithidae that were native to New Zealand; until its extinction, one species was the largest bird in the world. [from 19th c.]
A tree of species Baillonella toxisperma, found throughout subtropical forests of Africa, used for its oil.
One of the large stone statues on Easter Island (Rapa Nui).
A low, mournful cry of pain, sorrow or pleasure.
(intransitive) To make a moan or similar sound. [from 18th c.]
A deep, wide defensive ditch, normally filled with water, surrounding a fortified habitation.
(Australian Aboriginal) A group of Aboriginal people associated with an extended family group, clan group or wider community group, from a particular place or country.
(biology) Capable of being moved, aroused, or excited; capable of spontaneous movement.
(sculpture) A kinetic sculpture or decorative arrangement made of items hanging so that they can move independently from each other.
(video games) An electronic game played using a cellular phone.
Mobile phone number. [from 1940s]
A portable telephone that connects with the cellular telephone network
(telecommunications) All the user equipment (mobile phone, SIM card etc) and software needed for communication with a GSM network.
(transitive) To assemble troops and their equipment in a coordinated fashion so as to be ready for war.
The ability to move; capacity for movement. [from 15th c.]
(military) The ability of a military unit to move or be transported to a new position. [from 18th c.]
(chiefly, sociology) The ability of people to move between different social levels or professional occupations. [from 19th c.]
An electric-powered scooter, similar in use to a wheelchair, that is specially designed for disabled and/or elderly people.
The marshalling and organizing of troops and national resources in preparation for war, bringing them to a state of readiness for an action.
Rule or control by the mob (or by the mass of ordinary people); a mob as a politically powerful force.

A traditional Native North American shoe, usually without a heel or sole, made of a piece of deerskin or other soft leather turned up at the edges which are either stitched together at the top of the shoe, or sewn to a vamp (a piece covering the top of the foot). [from early 17th c.]
A modern shoe with either a low or no heel resembling a traditional Native American moccasin in that the leather forming the sides of the shoe is stitched at the top.
(countable) A coffee drink with chocolate syrup added, or a serving thereof.
A small Japanese rice cake made from glutinous rice.
Japanese rice flour
An imitation, usually of lesser quality.
Mockery; the act of mocking.
To mimic, to simulate.
To make fun of, especially by mimicking; to taunt.
especially, Philadelphus coronarius (sweet mock orange), widely cultivated
A scale or full-size model of a design or device which is not fully functional, used for teaching, demonstration, design evaluation, promotion, or other purposes.
Any of various long-tailed American songbirds of the genera Mimus and Melanotis, noted for their ability to mimic calls of other birds.
A non-alcoholic cocktail.
(linguistics) a word class that indicates the mood of an utterance
(computing) One of various related sets of rules for processing data; more generally, any state of the system associated with certain behaviours.
A particular means of accomplishing something.
Any form of vehicle or system used to transport people or goods.
A person who serves as a human template for artwork or fashion.
A representation of a physical object.
A style, type, or design.
The structural design of a complex system.
A successful example to be copied, with or without modifications.
(software architecture) In software applications using the model-view-controller design pattern, the part or parts of the application that manage the data.
A malleable substance used in building models and sculpting.
(computing) A device that encodes digital computer signals into analog telephone signals and vice versa, allowing computers to communicate over a phone line.
Not excessive; acting in moderation
One who holds an intermediate position between extremes, as in politics.
Pertaining to a current or recent time and style; not ancient.
An athletics event where athletes compete in épée fencing, shooting, freestyle swimming, show jumping and cross country.
Any of several styles of art, architecture, literature, philosophy, etc., that flourished in the 20th century.
The process of modernizing.
(transitive) To make (something old or outdated) up to date, or modern in style or function by adding or changing equipment, designs, etc.
Not bragging or boasting about oneself or one's achievements; unpretentious, humble.
Small, moderate in size.
A modest, small, or trifling amount.
The act of making a change to something while keeping its essential character intact; an alteration or adjustment. [from 18th c.]
Any of various products, prepared by physical or chemical treatment of starch, that are used as food additives

(grammar) A word, phrase, or clause that limits or qualifies the sense of another word or phrase. (It may be any of the following: an adjective phrase, an adverb phrase, a prepositional phrase, a noun phrase, or a subordinate clause.)
(transitive, grammar) To qualify the meaning of.

(engineering, physics, uncountable) Chiefly preceded by a descriptive word: modification of an electromagnetic wave or other oscillating carrier wave to apply a signal to it; (countable) an instance of this; also, the extent to which such a wave is modified; and the modified wave or signal.
A device or thing that modulates.
A self-contained component of a system, often interchangeable, which has a well-defined interface to the other components.
(fandom slang) Strong interest in, and especially fetishistic attraction towards, fictional characters in anime, manga, video games, and/or similar media.
The long, fine hair of the Angora goat.
A Burmese soup made with rice noodles and fish.
Characterized by the presence of moisture; not dry; slightly wet; damp. [from 14th c.]
(informal) Of the vagina: sexually lubricated due to sexual arousal; of a woman: sexually aroused, turned on. [from 20th c.]
The state of being moist.
(computing) Corrupt characters or letters, especially resulting from being displayed or transferred through an inappropriate character set or encoding.
A Cuban cocktail, generally made from rum, lime, sugar, mint, etc.

In Indian philosophy and theology, the final liberation of the soul or consciousness from samsara and the bringing to an end of all the suffering involved in being subject to the cycle of reincarnation.
A back tooth having a broad surface used for grinding one's food.
A thick, sweet syrup drained from sugarcane, especially (North America) the still thicker and sweeter syrup produced by boiling down raw molasses.
A natural substance in the form of a furry or woolly growth of tiny fungi that appears when organic material lies for a long time exposed to (usually warm and moist) air.
A naevus, a pigmented, slightly raised, and sometimes hairy spot on the skin.
Any of several small, burrowing, insectivorous mammals of the family Talpidae.
(espionage) An internal spy; a person who involves themself with an enemy organisation, especially an intelligence or governmental organisation, to determine and betray its secrets from within.
(nautical) A massive structure, usually of stone, used as a pier, breakwater or junction between places separated by water.

(chemistry, physics) In the International System of Units, the base unit of amount of substance; the amount of substance of a system which contains exactly 6.02214076×1023 elementary entities (atoms, ions, molecules, etc.). Symbol: mol. The number of atoms is known as Avogadro’s number. [from 1897]
Any of various large insects from the family Gryllotalpidae that burrow into moist soil and feed on plant roots.
(biochemistry, genetics) a scientist who specializes in molecular biology
(genetics) The branch of biology that studies the manipulation of genetic sequence of DNA.
(chemistry) A notation indicating the number of atoms of each element present in one molecule of a substance.
A field of biology which studies the structure and function of genes at a molecular level.
(chemistry) The mass of an individual molecule of an element or compound.

(physical chemistry, quantum mechanics) The quantum mechanical behavior of an electron in a molecule describing the probability of the electron's particular position and energy; approximated by a linear combination of atomic orbitals.
(chemistry) The smallest particle of a specific element or compound that retains the chemical properties of that element or compound; two or more atoms held together by chemical bonds.
A small mound of earth created by a mole's burrowing underneath the surface of the ground.
One who molests.
A soft-bodied invertebrate of the phylum Mollusca, typically with a hard shell of one or more pieces.
A chemical element (symbol Mo) with an atomic number of 42: a silvery metal, not found as a free element, used in steel alloys.
(physics, mechanics) Ellipsis of moment of force.
(historical, unit) A definite period of time, specifically one-tenth of a point, or one-fortieth or one-fiftieth of an hour.
(math) An infinitesimal change in a varying quantity; an increment or decrement.
(colloquial, Internet slang, of a person) The current center of public attention and awe; the most important celebrity in their prime.

A period of silence conducted to honor or provide a gesture of respect to a recently deceased person, as part of the mourning process. May also be conducted following a tragic event or on the anniversary thereof.
(manner) In a momentary manner; for a moment or instant.
(US, proscribed, duration) In a moment or very soon; any minute now, any time now.
Outstanding in importance, of great consequence.
A unit of weight (3.75 grams) used for pearls, paper, and silk.
(slang, by extension) Any sexually attractive woman.
A type of dumpling from Nepal, Ladakh or Tibet made with a simple flour and water dough and filled with meat, vegetables or cheese.
The ruler of an absolute monarchy or the head of state of a constitutional monarchy.
A butterfly of the species Danaus plexippus, native to North and Central America.
The advocacy of such a political system.
A government in which sovereignty is embodied within a single, today usually hereditary head of state (whether as a figurehead or as a powerful ruler).
A residence for monks or others who have taken religious vows.

cit.quote: ヒレジロマンザイウオ

sense.def: (Hawaii) Sickle pomfret (Taractichthys steindachneri)
(Hawaii) Brilliant pomfret (also called lustrous pomfret, Eumegistus illustris)
(linguistics) A form of (possibly intentional) error arising from mishearing a spoken or sung phrase, possibly in a different language. [from 1954]
Of, pertaining to, or consisting of money.
A standard unit of a currency, of which the value of coins or notes are multiples
A currency maintained by a state or other entity which can guarantee its value (such as a monetary union).
Hard cash in the form of banknotes and coins, as opposed to cheques/checks, credit cards, or credit more generally.
(in the plural) A wealthy person.

cit.quote: お金は幸福を買わない

sense.def: Money can purchase external things, but true happiness comes from within oneself.

cit.quote: マネー・ロンダリング
マネー・ローンダリング

sense.def: The act of engaging in transactions designed to obscure the origin of money, especially money that has been obtained illegally. [from early 20th c.]
(banking, finance) A directive to pay a prespecified amount of money from prepaid funds, making it a more trusted method of payment than a check.

cit.quote: 閻魔大王が下す地獄での判決も金次第では軽くもなる

sense.def: Money or moneyed interests have power.
(informal) A wealthy person.
A dealer or trader in a specific commodity.

(anthropology, dated) A member of the racial classification of humanity composed of peoples native to North Asia, East Asia, Southeast Asia, Pacific Oceania, the Americas, and parts of Central Asia and South Asia (and sometimes eastern Fennoscandia) – as well as their descendants in other parts of the world.

Any of several species of generalist predatory carnivores in the family Herpestidae; the various species range in size from rats to large cats. Indian mongooses are predators of venomous snakes, though other mongoose species have similar habits.
(often, pejorative) Someone or something of mixed kind or uncertain origin, especially a dog.
(philosophy, religion) The doctrine of the oneness and unity of reality, despite the appearance of diversity in the world.
(computing) A device similar to a television set used as to give a graphical display of the output from a computer.
Any of various large carnivorous lizards of the family Varanidae, all of whose extant species are of genus Varanus, native to Africa, Asia and Australia.
The carrying out of surveillance on, or continuous or regular observation of, an environment or people in order to detect signals, movements or changes of state or quality.
(loosely, sometimes, _, proscribed) Any simian primate other than hominids, any monkey or ape.
Activity that is mischievous, stupid, or time-wasting. [from mid 19th c.]
Activity that is morally questionable or even mildly illegal.
A wrench (spanner) with an adjustable jaw.
An enclosure in which monkeys are kept.
(informal) Monaural or monophonic; having only a single audio channel.
one, single, only
(sumo) a conference among the shimpan to reconsider a referee's decision
(enzyme) Either of two enzymes, found in the outer membrane of mitochondria, that degrade biogenic amines and are thus responsible for the destruction of transmitter substances at neuronal synapses.
Having only one colour.
(photography) Representing colours with shades of gray.
A black and white image, especially such a photograph.
A single lens, usually in a wire frame, and used to correct vision for only one eye.

(botany) Any plant whose seedlings typically have one cotyledon (seed leaf) (in contrast to the two cotyledons typical of dicots), thereby belonging to the taxonomic monocots, formerly variously known as Monocotyledones, Monocotyledonae, or Liliopsida, a class in the angiosperms (Angiospermae), the flowering plants.
(chiefly, anime, and, manga) A humanlike monster girl with a single large eye.
(narrowly) Being married to one person at a time.
A form of sexual bonding involving a permanent pair bond between two beings.
A design or motif composed of one or more letters, often intertwined, used as an identifying mark of an individual or institution; the letters are usually the initials of their names.
A scholarly book or a treatise on a single subject or a group of related subjects, usually written by one person.
The worship of a single deity (possibly while believing in the existence of others).
Knowing or using a single language; written or spoken in a single language.

(also, attributively) A large, single block of stone which is a natural feature; or a block of stone or other similar material used in architecture and sculpture, especially one carved into a monument in ancient times.
(also, attributively, and, figurative) Anything massive, uniform, and unmovable, especially a towering and impersonal cultural, political, or social organization or structure.
(engineering) Consisting of a single piece of homogeneous material as opposed to a composite material or an assembly of multiple parts.
(figurative) Having a massive, unchanging structure that does not permit individual variation.
(drama, authorship) A long speech by one person in a play; sometimes a soliloquy; other times spoken to other characters.
(comedy) A long series of comic stories and jokes as an entertainment.
(chemistry) A relatively small molecule which can be covalently bonded to other monomers to form a polymer or oligomer.
(pathology) A viral infection marked by extreme fatigue, high fever, and swollen lymph nodes.

A vowel (in the sense of a sound rather than a letter of the alphabet) that has the same sound throughout its pronunciation, such as the short vowels in "pap", "pep", "pip", "pop" and "pup", as opposed to a diphthong (eg, /aɪ/, the vowel in "pipe") or a triphthong (eg, /aɪə/, the sound in the non-rhotic pronunciation of "pyre").

(Christianity) A Christological doctrine, generally considered heterodox or heretical, holding that Jesus Christ has a single nature, which is either wholly divine or partially human and partially divine.
(aviation) An airplane that has a single pair of wings.
An exclusive control over the trade or production of a commodity or service through exclusive possession.
(economics) A market situation in which there is only one buyer for a product. [from 1930s]
a railroad system where the trains run on one rail
(carbohydrate) A simple sugar such as glucose, fructose or deoxyribose that has a single ring

cit.quote: グルタミン酸ナトリウム

sense.def: (chemistry) The mono sodium salt of the amino acid, glutamic acid; present in soy sauce; used as a condiment in Chinese and Japanese cooking, and as a food additive to enhance flavor and add the umami taste. Abbreviations: MSG, E621.
Consisting of one syllable.
The belief in a single deity (one god or goddess); especially within an organized religion.
Having an unvarying pitch or tone.
Tedious, repetitious, or lacking in variety.
(zoology) Any of the order Monotremata of mammals that lay eggs and have single orifices for urogenital and digestive functions (cloaca); an echidna, platypus or one of their extinct relatives.
A fleshy protuberance over the pubic bones that becomes covered with hair during puberty.
Any of a number of winds associated with regions where most rain falls during a particular season.
Tropical rainy season when the rain lasts for several months with few interruptions.
Entire meteorological systems with such characteristics.
A terrifying and dangerous creature, especially one of an imaginary or mythical kind.
A very large penis.
(anime, and, manga) A fictional female character who shares visual traits with a monster.
A large truck designed specifically to perform in monster truck shows, typically based on a lifted pickup truck with oversized wheels and modified suspension.
(Christianity) An ornamental, often precious receptacle, either open or with a transparent cover, in which the sacramental bread (consecrated host) is placed for Eucharistic adoration.
A monstrous person, thing, or act.
(countable) A composite work, particularly an artwork, created by assembling or putting together other elements such as pieces of music, pictures, texts, videos, etc. [from early 20th c.]
(ecology) Of, inhabiting, or growing in mountain areas; specifically, the cool, moist upland slopes below the timberline. [from mid 19th c.]
A period into which a year is divided, historically based on the phases of the moon.
Occurring every month.
Every month.
A publication that is published once a month.
(archaic) Resembling a mountain in form.
A structure built for commemorative or symbolic reasons, or as a memorial; a commemoration.
The characteristic sound made by a cow or bull.
(childish) A cow.
(mostly, pejorative) A person having a tendency to take advantage of the help of others, especially if making little effort to help themselves.
A mental or emotional state, composure.
Dour, gloomy or brooding.
A book published in the form factor of a magazine.
(informal, by extension of Moon) Any natural satellite of a planet.
(literary) A month, particularly a lunar month.
(nautical, chiefly, oil industry) An opening in the base of the hull of a vessel (especially a marine drilling platform), which is used for lowering equipment into the sea below.
(originally, scifi) A base or outpost located on a moon.
A shaft of moonlight.
(meteorology) A rainbow formed by moonlight diffracted by water droplets in the air, usually fainter than a daytime rainbow and with fewer distinguishable colours.

A rich, dense Chinese pastry traditionally filled with lotus seed paste and nowadays with a variety of other fillings, usually eaten during the Mid-Autumn Festival (on the 15th day of the eighth month of the Chinese lunisolar calendar; early September to early October). [from late 17th c.]
Mene maculata, of tropical coastal waters of the Indo-Pacific area.
Any of several vines of the genus Ipomoea, especially Ipomoea alba. [from 19th c.]
(sometimes, attributive) The light reflected from the Moon.

cit.quote: 月明かりに照らされた

sense.def: Lit by moonlight.
A seismic event occurring on the moon; the lunar equivalent of an earthquake.
(math, uncountable) A branch of pure mathematics relating the Monster group to an invariant of elliptic functions.
(mineral) A translucent gemstone, an orthoclase feldspar, that has a pearly lustre.
(dance) A dance style in which the dancer appears to be moving in a low gravity environment.
A small fern, Botrychium lunaria (lesser moonwort); later, any member of the genus. [from 15th c.]
(now, _, US, UK, _, regional) Lunaria annua (greater moonwort); also known as honesty and annual honesty. [from 16th c.]
An extensive waste covered with patches of heath, and having a poor, light (and usually acidic) soil, but sometimes marshy, and abounding in peat; a heath. (Compare bog, peatland, marsh, swamp, fen.)
(intransitive, nautical) To cast anchor or become fastened.
(transitive, nautical) To fix or secure (e.g. a vessel) in a particular place by casting anchor, or by fastening with ropes, cables or chains or the like.
The largest member of the deer family (Alces americanus, sometimes included in Alces alces), of which the male has very large, palmate antlers.
An implement for washing floors or similar, made of a piece of cloth, or a collection of thrums, or coarse yarn, fastened to a handle.
A lightweight, two-wheeled vehicle equipped with a small motor and pedals, designed to go no faster than some specified speed limit.
(phonology) A unit of syllable weight used in phonology, by which stress, foot structure, or timing of utterance is determined in some languages (e.g. Japanese).
(geology) An accumulation of rocks and debris carried and deposited by a glacier.
Of or relating to principles of right and wrong in behaviour, especially for teaching right behaviour.
(of a narrative) The ethical significance or practical lesson.
(ethics) A written, formal, and consistent set of rules prescribing righteous behavior, accepted by a person or by a group of people.
A semi-spontaneous or media-generated mass movement based on the perception that an individual, group, community, or culture is dangerously deviant and poses a menace to society; a public outcry.
(philosophy) Ethics.
The capacity of people to maintain belief in an institution or a goal, or even in oneself and others.

(uncountable) Recognition of the distinction between good and evil or between right and wrong; respect for and obedience to the rules of right conduct; the mental disposition or characteristic of behaving in a manner intended to produce morally good results.
(legal) An authorization to a debtor, permitting temporary suspension of payments. [from 19th c.]
Any of the large cosmopolitan carnivorous eels of the family Muraenidae.
(originally) Of, relating to, or afflicted by disease. [from 1650s]
(by extension) Taking an interest in, or fixating on, unhealthy or unwholesome subjects such as death, decay, disease. [from 1770s]
(music) An ornament consisting of a single alternation between a given pitch and the one immediately below it.
Used to form the comparative form of adjectives and adverbs. [from 13thc.]
in greater number. (Used for a discrete quantity.)
in greater quantity, amount, or proportion. (Used for a continuous quantity.)
Additional; further.
Bigger, stronger, or more valuable.
(degree) Progressively more.
(idiom) Usually; more than half the time; more likely to be the case than not to be the case.
Approximately.
Almost.
To varying extents, across instances; to an extent that varies among cases.
A true morel; any of several fungi in the genus Morchella, the upper part of which is covered with a reticulated and pitted hymenium.
(conjunctive) In addition to what has been said.

cit.quote: ニュージーランドアオバズク

sense.def: (chiefly, New Zealand) The Tasmanian spotted owl (Ninox novaeseelandiae), a small brown owl indigenous to New Zealand and Tasmania. [from 19th c.]
A set of moral norms or customs derived from generally accepted practices rather than written laws.
A building or room where dead bodies are kept before their proper burial or cremation, (now) particularly in legal and law enforcement contexts.
Approaching death; about to die; dying; expiring.
A traditional Mongolian bowed stringed instrument.
(historical) A kind of open brimmed helmet used by footsoldiers in the 16th and 17th centuries, having no visor or bevor. [from 16th c.]
The early part of the day, especially from midnight to noon. [from 13th c.]
(obsolete) That part of the day from dawn until the main meal (typically in late afternoon). [18th–19th c.]
Several members of the family Convolvulaceae; climbing plants with trumpet shaped flowers.
(medicine) Early morning nausea and vomiting as a symptom of pregnancy.
(countable, weapon) A weapon consisting of a heavy ball set with spikes attached rigidly to a staff, in contrast to a flail.
(astronomy) The planet Venus as observed in the eastern sky around dawn.
(dialectal) Kindling used to light a fire in the morning.
(psychology, dated, originally) A person of mild mental subnormality in the former classification of mental retardation, having an intelligence quotient of 50–70.
(linguistic morphology) The smallest linguistic unit within a word that can carry a meaning. It may be a letter, a syllable, or otherwise.

(biochemistry, pharmaceutical drug) A crystalline alkaloid (4,5-epoxy-17-methyl-7,8-didehydromorphinan-3,6-diol), extracted from opium, the salts of which are soluble in water and are used as analgesics, anaesthetics and sedatives; it is one of a group of morphine alkaloids.

(mathematics, category theory) (formally) An arrow in a category; (less formally) an abstraction that generalises a map from one mathematical object to another and is structure-preserving in a way that depends on the branch of mathematics from which it arises.
(organic compound) A six-membered, saturated heterocycle tetrahydro-1,4-oxazine containing four carbon atoms, one nitrogen and one oxygen atom; it has a number of industrial applications.
(biology) The study of the form and structure of animals and plants.
(uncountable) A scientific study of form and structure, usually without regard to function. Especially:
(linguistics) The study of the internal structure of morphemes (words and their semantic building blocks).
(linguistics) The system of the internal structure of words (morphology) and the way in which words are put together to form phrases and sentences (syntax), regarded as an interlinked unit.
A smooth-textured Italian pork sausage with lumps of fat, flavoured with spices; eaten cold.
Susceptible to death by aging, sickness, injury, or wound; not immortal. [from 14th c.]
Causing death; deadly, fatal, killing, lethal (now only of wounds, injuries etc.). [from 14th c.]
Affecting as if with power to kill; deathly.
A human; someone susceptible to death.

(Roman Catholicism, theology) A sin which causes the loss of God's grace, leading to eternal damnation, unless the sinner repents, which includes their intent to confess and atone; such a sin is defined as a grave transgression against one of the Ten Commandments with the full knowledge and deliberate consent of the sinner.
The state of being susceptible to death.
The number of deaths; and, usually and especially, the number of deaths per time unit (usually per year), expressed as a rate.
(figuratively) Death.
(uncountable) A mixture of lime or cement, sand and water used for bonding building blocks.
(countable) A hollow vessel used to pound, crush, rub, grind or mix ingredients with a pestle.

(countable, military) A relatively lightweight, often portable indirect fire weapon which transmits recoil to a base plate and is designed to lob explosive shells at very steep trajectories. [from 20th c.]

(legal) A special form of secured loan where the purpose of the loan must be specified to the lender, to purchase assets that must be fixed (not movable) property, such as a house or piece of farm land. The assets are registered as the legal property of the borrower but the lender can seize them and dispose of them if they are not satisfied with the manner in which the repayment of the loan is conducted by the borrower. Once the loan is fully repaid, the lender loses this right of seizure and the assets are then deemed to be unencumbered.
A sensation of extreme shame or embarrassment.
(medicine) The death of part of the body.
(transitive) To discipline (one's body, appetites etc.) by suppressing desires; to practise abstinence on. [from 15th c.]
(transitive, usually, used passively) To injure the dignity of; to embarrass; to humiliate. [from 17th c.]
(obsolete, transitive) To reduce the potency of; to nullify; to deaden, neutralize. [14th–18th c.]
(archaic, transitive) To kill off (living tissue etc.); to make necrotic. [15th–18th c.]
(woodworking) A hole that is made to receive a tenon so as to form a joint. [from 14th c.]
A piece of artwork created by placing colored squares (usually tiles) in a pattern so as to create a picture.
(genetics) An individual composed of two or more cell lines of different genetic or chromosomal constitution, but from the same zygote.
(plant disease) Any of several viral diseases that cause mosaic-like patterns to appear on leaves.
A composite picture made from overlapping photographs.
The chemical element with atomic number 115.
The spontaneous dance floor created in front of a stage when people mosh.
(Islam) A place of worship for Muslims, often having at least one minaret; a masjid.

A small flying insect of the family Culicidae, the females of which bite humans and animals and suck blood, leaving an itching bump on the skin, and sometimes carrying diseases like malaria, dengue and yellow fever.
A mosquito-repelling incense, usually shaped into a spiral, and typically made from a dried paste of pyrethrum powder.
A fine net, placed around a bed, in a window opening, etc., to provide protection against mosquitoes and other insects, and the diseases carried by them.
Any of various small, green, seedless plants growing on the ground or on the surfaces of trees, stones, etc.; now specifically, a plant of the phylum Bryophyta (formerly division Musci).
A dark green colour with a tint of yellow, like that of moss.
A pale greyish green color, like that of lichen.
Forms the superlative of many adjectives.
the comparatively largest number of (construed with the definite article)

(transitive) To bring peace to (a place or situation), by ending war, fighting, violence, anger or agitation.
A bundle made up and prepared to be carried; especially, a bundle to be carried on the back, but also a load for an animal, a bale.
A group of hounds or dogs, hunting or kept together.
(transitive) To make a pack of; to arrange closely and securely in a pack; hence, to place and arrange compactly as in a pack
(physical) To put or bring things together in a limited or confined space, especially for storage or transport.
(of things) To put into bags to prepare to move.
Something which is packed, a parcel, a box, an envelope.
(software) A piece of software which has been prepared in such a way that it can be installed with a package manager.
(uncountable, archaic) The act of packing something.
To pack or bundle something.
To prepare (a book, a television series, etc.), including all stages from research to production, in order to sell the result to a publisher or broadcaster.
(chiefly, UK, Ireland, Commonwealth) A holiday that consists of transport and accommodation advertised and sold together by a vendor known as a tour operator.
(simile, informal) Densely packed; tightly squeezed together; crammed.
A meal, sandwiches or anything packed and intended to be eaten away from home; especially, one packed at home as opposed to a portable packaged lunch from a vendor.
A small pack or package; a little bundle or parcel
An agreement; a compact; a covenant.
A traditional Polish doughnut.
A flattened mass of anything soft, to sit or lie on.
A cushion-like thickening of the skin on the underside of the toes of animals.
A Thai dish of stir-fried noodles with egg, tamarind, peanuts and other ingredients.
An apprentice or student Jedi.

A two-handed implement consisting of a shaft with one or two blades attached to the end(s) used to propel a canoe, kayak or a small boat. A paddle is unattached to the boat and freely operated with the hands, compared with an oar which is attached to the boat at a pivot point.
A double-bladed version with blades at each end of the shaft is used for kayaking.
The use of a paddle to propel a boat; a session of paddling.
A slat of a paddleboat's wheel.
A paddlewheel.
A blade of a waterwheel.
A kitchen utensil shaped like a paddle and used for mixing, beating etc.
A flat limb of an aquatic animal, adapted for swimming.
In a sluice, a panel that controls the flow of water.
(transitive) To propel something through water with a paddle, oar, hands, etc.
(transitive) To spank with a paddle.
(watercraft) A steam-powered vessel propelled by one or two paddle wheels
Any of several primitive fish, of the family Polyodontidae, that have a long snout shaped like a paddle.
Rough or unhusked rice, either before it is milled or as a crop to be harvested. [from 17th c.]
(countable) A paddy field, a rice paddy; an irrigated or flooded field where rice is grown. [from 20th c.]
Acrocephalus agricola, a species of marsh warbler (family Acrocephalidae).
A detachable lock that can be used to secure something by means of a sliding or hinged shackle
(by extension) Any loud and joyous song; a song of triumph.
(by extension) An enthusiastic expression of praise.
A savory Valencian dish made of rice, cooked in a frying pan with vegetables and meat or shellfish.
A person not adhering to a main world religion; a follower of a pantheistic or nature-worshipping religion.
Any of a class of religions often associated with nature rituals.
One of the many pieces of paper bound together within a book or similar document.
(historical) A serving boy; a youth attending a person of high degree, especially at courts, often as a position of honor and education.
(computing) A screenful of text and possibly other content; especially, the digital simulation of one side of a paper leaf.
An elaborate public display, especially a parade in historical or traditional costume.
(now, frequently, historical) A boy who serves as a page. [from 19th c.]
(telecommunications) A wireless telecommunications device that receives text or voice messages.
A religious building in South and Southeast Asia, especially a multi-storey tower erected as a Hindu or Buddhist temple. [from 16th c.]

A form of lava flow of basaltic rock, usually dark-colored with a smooth or ropey surface. It is one of two chief forms of lava flow emitted from volcanoes of the Hawaiian type, the other form being aa.
(countable, and, uncountable) An ache or bodily suffering, or an instance of this; an unpleasant sensation, resulting from a derangement of functions, disease, or injury by violence; hurt.
(uncountable) The condition or fact of suffering or anguish especially mental, as opposed to pleasure; torment; distress
(countable, from, _, pain in the neck) An annoying person or thing.
(transitive) To hurt; to put to bodily uneasiness or anguish; to afflict with uneasy sensations of any degree of intensity; to torment; to torture.
(transitive) To render uneasy in mind; to disquiet; to distress; to grieve.
Causing pain or distress, either physical or mental. [from 14th c.]
Afflicted or suffering with pain (of a body part or, formerly, of a person). [from 15th c.]
Requiring effort or labor; difficult, laborious. [from 15th c.]
(pharmaceutical drug) A drug that numbs the pain in the body.
Free from pain; without pain or trouble.
Carefully attentive to details; studious; diligent in performing a process or procedure.
(dated) Any substance fixed with latex to harden it.
(transitive) To apply paint to.
(transitive) To apply in the manner that paint is applied.
(transitive, medicine) To apply with a brush in order to treat some body part.
(intransitive) To practise the art of painting pictures.
A solvent used to thin oil-based paints or clean up after their use.
(countable) The dye-filled capsule fired in the sport of paintball.
A thin brush for applying paint.
A brightly-colored finch (Passerina ciris) of the southern United States
An artist who paints pictures.
(obsolete) A chain or rope used to attach the shank of an anchor to the side of a ship when not in use. [14th–17th c.]
(nautical) A rope that is attached to the bow of a dinghy, or other small boat, and used for tying up or towing. [from 17th c.]
the action of applying paint
artistic application of paint
an illustration or artwork using paint
Two people in a relationship, partnership or friendship.
A couple of working animals attached to work together, as by a yoke.

(kinematics) In a mechanism, two elements, or bodies, which are so applied to each other as to mutually constrain relative motion; named in accordance with the motion it permits, as in turning pair, sliding pair, twisting pair.

A tool for drawing accurate circles or circular arcs, or for measuring or transferring lengths, usually consisting of two arms joined with an adjustable hinge at one end; until the middle ages both arms always had metal points at their free ends (this version is now called a divider or pair of dividers), but in recent centuries for a device called a compass or pair of compasses, one arm typically holds a ruling pen, pencil, or some other implement for making marks.
A motif of a swirling droplet.
(historical) A tablet of authority in the Mongol Empire.
Clothes for wearing to bed and sleeping in, usually consisting of a loose-fitting shirt and pants/trousers.
A Korean pancake made with green onions.
A large and lavishly ornate residence.
The scientific study of prehistoric climate of the Earth.
The study of historical geography — of the (chiefly physical, but sometimes political/cultural) geography of the world in the geologic past.
(loosely) Synonym of litter, any similar vehicle open or closed, human or animal-borne, particularly (historical) in colonial Asian contexts.
(phonology, uncountable) The state or quality of being palatalized, of pronouncing a sound with the tongue against the palate of the mouth that normally is not.
(phonology, countable) An instance of pronunciation in which a sound is palatalized.
(anatomy) The roof of the mouth, separating the cavities of the mouth and nose in vertebrates. [from 14th c.]
Light in color.
(heraldiccharge) A vertical band down the middle of a shield.
A thrush (Turdus pallidus), of eastern Asia.
Old; ancient or primitive.
(anthropology) The scientific study of ancient human remains.
The branch of biology or paleontology concerned with the study of fossils of plants and animals
The branch of paleontology that deals with the study of plant fossils. [from Template:SAFESUBST: c.]
(US politics) Holding views associated with paleoconservatism.

(US politics) A political conservative who espouses paleoconservatism, opposing mass immigration, embracing states' rights and supporting cultural conservatism and social structures perceived to be traditional.
The study of old or ancient forms of writing.
A word or phrase that was coined in the distant past, often now obscured or offensive, or if recently used: possibly having a definition or implication different from that of any earlier usage.
(American spelling) The study of the forms of life existing in prehistoric or geologic times, especially as represented by fossils.
(painting) A thin board on which a painter lays and mixes colours.
In painting, a small, edge-less, more or less flexible steel blade used to mix paint on a palette and sometimes to apply paint to a surface.
(historical) A small horse with a smooth, ambling gait, popular in the Middle Ages with nobles and women for riding (contrasted with a warhorse).

A word, phrase, number or any other sequence of units which has the property of reading the same forwards as it does backwards, character for character, sometimes disregarding punctuation, capitalization and diacritics.
A fence made of palings.
An ode or other poem in which the author retracts something said in an earlier poem; (loosely) a recantation. [from 17th c.]
A chemical element (symbol Pd) with an atomic number of 46: a rare, lustrous silvery-white metal.
One called upon to carry or bear the coffin or the casket at a funeral.
A portable platform, usually designed to be easily moved by a forklift, on which goods can be stacked, for transport or storage.
(medicine) Minimising the progression of a disease and relieving undesirable symptoms for as long as possible, rather than attempting to cure the (usually incurable) disease.
A specialized area of healthcare that focuses on relieving and preventing the suffering of patients.
The inner and somewhat concave part of the human hand or other primate hand that extends from the wrist to the bases of the fingers.
(historical) Synonym of hand, any of various units of length notionally derived from the breadth of the palm, formalized in England as 4 inches and now chiefly used for the height of horses
(historical) Any of various units of length notionally derived from the length of the palm from the wrist to the base of the fingers.
To hold or conceal something in the palm of the hand, e.g., for an act of sleight of hand or to steal something.
To hold something without bending the fingers significantly.
A solid form of the vegetable oil obtained from the fruit of oil palms.
An edible plant oil derived from the mesocarp (reddish pulp) of the fruit of the oil palm (Elaeis guineensis).
Sugar made from the sap of various species of palm tree, family Arecaceae.
A tree of the family Arecaceae usually characterised by having a single stem or trunk, directly from which sprout several leaves or fronds giving a shape like an outstretched hand.
Any alcoholic drink produced from the sap of palm trees; toddy.
A fortuneteller who uses palmistry.
Telling fortunes from the lines on the palms of the hand.
(fatty acid) One of the most common saturated fatty acids; it is found in all animal and most vegetable oils and fats; it is used in the manufacture of soap etc.
A palm (Borassus flabellifer) with straight black upright trunk and palmate leaves, whose wood, fruit, and roots can be used for many purposes.
To examine or otherwise explore through touch, particularly (medical) in reference to an area or organ of the human body.
An abnormal beating of the heart that may be perceived by the patient, a result of excitement, exertion, or illness.
Trashy, trivial, of little value.
Of little monetary worth.
(transitive) To treat with excessive care, attention or indulgence.

A small, brief printed work, consisting either of a folded sheet of paper, or several sheets bound together into a booklet with only a paper cover, formerly containing literary compositions, newsletters, and newspapers, but now chiefly informational matter.

(uncountable, film) The method or practice of adjusting widescreen film images, especially 2.35:1 or 2.39:1 aspect ratio, so that they can be shown within the proportions of a 1.33:1 or 1.78:1 aspect ratio television screen, by cropping off sides of the original widescreen image, as opposed to letterboxing.
Encompassing, including all, or involving all.
The belief in unification of the peoples and countries of the Arab World.
A remedy believed to cure all disease and prolong life that was originally sought by alchemists; a cure-all.
(politics) Advocacy of panarchy.
(countable, and, uncountable) A thin batter cake fried in a pan or on a griddle in oil or butter; in particular:
In the US (and e.g. Scotland), a leavened, thicker, fluffier cake.
(anatomy) A gland near the stomach which secretes a fluid into the duodenum to assist with food digestion.
(oncology, disease) A malignant neoplasm of the pancreas.
(colloquial, also, attributively) Ellipsis of giant panda (“Ailuropoda melanoleuca”). [from 19th c.]

A type of hand-held frame drum with a round wooden frame and six pairs of metal discs fit along the sides, and an animal skin or nylon head; similar to a tambourine but with head tension that can be tuned and crisper, drier, and less sustained jingles, used in a number of Brazilian music forms.

(religion) A belief in a god who is both pantheistic and deistic, in particular a god who designed the universe and then became it and ceased to exist separately and act consciously with respect to it.
(epidemiology) A pandemic disease; a disease that affects a wide geographical area and a large proportion of the population.
A sweet bread loaf of Veronese origin, in the shape of a star, traditionally eaten at Christmas.
A soft, non-matured, Indian cheese.
A formal speech publicly praising someone or something.
A (usually) rectangular section of a surface, or of a covering or of a wall, fence etc.
A group of people gathered to judge, interview, discuss etc. as on a television or radio broadcast for example.
A soft Italian sourdough brioche from Milan, with candied fruit, usually prepared for Christmas as a dessert.
A dense flat cake, a speciality of Siena, made with honey, hazelnuts, almonds, candied fruit, cocoa and spices.
Any of several long-tailed, scale-covered mammals of the family Manidae within the order Pholidota of tropical Africa and Asia.
A sentence that contains every letter of the alphabet.
(uncountable) Overwhelming fear or fright, often affecting groups of people or animals; (countable) an instance of this; a fright, a scare.
To cause (someone) to feel panic; also, to frighten (someone) into acting hastily.
A sudden period of intense anxiety, mounting physiological arousal, fear, stomach problems and discomfort that are associated with a variety of somatic and cognitive symptoms.
In a state of panic.
a sandwich
A form of fried puff-pastry balls filled with a watery mixture of tamarind, chili, chaat masala, potato, onion and chickpeas, from India and Pakistan.
A northern Italian dessert consisting of flavoured double cream set with gelatine, often served with fruit sauce or caramel syrup.
A large basket or bag fastened, usually in pairs, to the back of a bicycle or pack animal, or carried in pairs over the shoulders.
(historical, fashion) One of a pair of hoops used to expand the volume of a woman's skirt to either side.
A type of prison where all the cells are visible from the center, particularly if it is not possible for those in a cell to know if they are being watched.
A room for the exhibition of novelties.
A picture or series of pictures representing a continuous scene.

(musical instrument) An instrument consisting of a series of ten or more tubes of different lengths, typically closed at the bottom and open at the top, and is played by blowing across the open end at the top.
(philosophy, metaphysics, uncountable) The doctrine that all matter has a mental aspect.
A sexual orientation characterized by the potential for aesthetic attraction, romantic love and/or sexual desire for people regardless of their gender or sex.
A cultivated flowering plant, derived by hybridization within species Viola tricolor.
A quick breathing; a catching of the breath; a gasp: the panting of animals such as a dog with their tong hung out- as a form of thermoregulation.
(ambitransitive) To breathe quickly or in a labored manner, as after exertion or from eagerness or excitement; to respire with heaving of the breast; to gasp.
(religion) The belief that the Universe is in some sense divine and should be revered. Pantheism identifies the universe with God but denies any personality or transcendence of such a God.
Any of various big cats with black fur; most especially, the black-coated leopard of Africa and Asia.
Any big cat of the genus Panthera.
The highly poisonous agaric Amanita pantherina.
Underpants for women and girls.
(rail transport) A similarly-formed conductive device, now usually Z-shaped, that collects electric current from overhead lines for trains and trams.

(UK) A traditional theatrical entertainment, originally based on the commedia dell'arte, but later aimed mostly at children and involving physical comedy, topical jokes, call and response, and fairy-tale plots. [from 18th c.]
The act of gesturing without speaking; a dumb-show, a mime. [from 18th c.]
A small room, closet, or cabinet usually located in or near the kitchen, dedicated to shelf-stable food storage or storing kitchenware, like a larder, but smaller.

(chiefly, North America, Australia, New Zealand, South Africa, India, Philippines) An outer garment that covers the body from the waist downwards, covering each leg separately, usually as far as the ankles; trousers. [from 19th c.]
(chiefly, UK) An undergarment that covers the genitals and often the buttocks and the neighbouring parts of the body; underpants. [from 19th c.]
A prank where a woman's underwear is stolen.

cit.quote: パンティストッキング

sense.def: A fur or sometimes wool hat traditionally worn by men throughout the Caucasus and Central Asia; its shape varies from hemispherical to cylindrical, which may be slightly tapered in either direction.
A freelance photographer who sells photographs of celebrities to the media, especially one who pursues celebrities and attempts to obtain candid photographs.
The fruit of this tree.
Made of paper.
A sheet material typically used for writing on or printing on (or as a non-waterproof container), usually made by draining cellulose fibres from a suspension in water.
A written document, generally shorter than a book; usually written as a school assignment or a government report.
(rock paper scissors) An open hand (a handshape resembling a sheet of paper), that beats rock and loses to scissors. It loses to lizard and beats Spock in rock-paper-scissors-lizard-Spock.
(finance, uncountable) Any financial assets other than specie, including paper money, commercial paper, and others.
(US) A toy airplane made by folding up a sheet of paper.
The 1st anniversary of some event, particularly a wedding.
A bag made of paper, especially a firm brown kind intended for carrying groceries.
(ceramics) Clay mixed with shredded paper or other fibres, valued for its strength and light weight in the production of large ceramic works.
A small, folded, wire or plastic device used to hold sheets of paper together.
A representation of the Japanese red-crowned crane made out of folded paper, a classic origami figure.
A disposable cup made out of paper and often lined with plastic or wax to prevent liquid from leaking out or soaking through the paper.
A disposable diaper made from paper and plastic, rather than cloth.
(rare, usually, NNSE) A person who has a driver's license but never drives.
A machine used to manufacture paper.
A factory devoted to making paper from wood pulp and other ingredients.
Cash in the form of banknotes.
A tree in the mulberry family (Moraceae), Broussonetia papyrifera, with fibrous inner bark used to make paper and tapa cloth.
(idiomatic) Something or someone that appears powerful, strong or threatening but is in reality weak, ineffective, or unable to withstand challenge.
(Britain) A sheet of absorbent paper dispensed in restrooms, usually used for drying washed hands.
