A species of spoonbill, Platalea ajaja.
The fleshy false fruit of a wild rose plant (e.g. sweetbrier, dog rose, burnet rose, etc.), containing the achenes or true fruits.
Hibiscus sabdariffa, an edible flower in the hibiscus family used to make hibiscus tea.
A shrub, Salvia rosmarinus (formerly Rosmarinus officinalis), that originates from Europe and Asia Minor and produces a fragrant herb used in cooking and perfumes.
A liquid produced by steeping rose petals in water, used as a coloring agent and a flavoring ingredient in certain foods.
(organic chemistry) A solid form of resin, obtained from liquid resin by vaporizing its volatile components.

A list of individuals or groups, usually for an organization of some kind such as military officers and enlisted personnel enrolled in a particular unit; a muster roll; a sports team, with the names of players who are eligible to be placed in the lineup for a particular game; or a list of students officially enrolled in a school or class.
The edentulous ossification that forms the ceratopsian beak.
A dais, pulpit, or similar platform for a speaker, conductor, or other performer.
Rose-coloured.
(countable) A serving of such wine.
A pale pink wine made by removing the dark grape skins at the required point during fermentation.
(intransitive) To suffer decomposition due to biological action, especially by fungi or bacteria.
(intransitive) To spin, turn, or revolve.
(transitive) To spin, turn, or revolve something.
(chiefly, uncountable) The act of turning around a centre or an axis.
(finance) Тhe movement of investments between different sectors of an economy, or styles of investing, based on anticipated changes in the economic or market cycle.
Any of a group of wheel-shaped viruses, of the genus Rotavirus, that causes gastroenteritis and diarrhea in children and animals.
Mechanical routine; a fixed, habitual, repetitive, or mechanical course of procedure.
A kind of unleavened flatbread commonly consumed in South Asia and the Caribbean.
Any of many minute aquatic multicellular organisms, of the phylum Rotifera, that have a ring of cilia resembling a wheel.
A rotating part of a mechanical device; for example, in an electric motor, generator, alternator, or pump. [from 1900s]

An amusement park and carnival ride consisting of a rotating cylindrical chamber in which centrifugal force adheres riders to the wall as the floor drops away, creating a sensation of defying gravity.
(film, TV, visual effects) A technique in which animators trace live-action movement frame by frame.
In a state of decay.
Bad or terrible.

(historical) A parliamentary borough that was represented in Parliament although the number of voters had diminished so greatly that they were largely controlled by the main landowner; such boroughs were abolished in the 19th century. [from mid 18th c.]
Not smooth; uneven.
Crude; unrefined.
A plant in the taxonomic genus Equisetum (horsetails); Equisetum hyemale.

(uncountable) A game of chance in which a small ball is made to move round rapidly on a circle divided off into numbered (usually red and black) spaces. When the ball stops, it indicates the result of a variety of wagers permitted by the game.
(cycle racing) A cyclist who performs well on flat and undulating roads.
(physical) Of shape:
Circular or cylindrical; having a circular cross-section in one direction.
Complete, whole, not lacking.
A circular or spherical object or part of an object.
(sports) One of the specified pre-determined segments of the total time of a sport event, such as a boxing or wrestling match, during which contestants compete before being signaled to stop.
(sports) In some sports, e.g. golf or showjumping: one complete way around the course.
A series of changes or events ending where it began; a series of like events recurring in continuance; a cycle; a periodical revolution.
(geometry) An angle of 360 degrees; a full circle.
(UK) Each of the signs ( and ); parenthesis, bracket (in a strict sense).
(mathematics, transitive, intransitive) To change (a number) to an approximation having fewer significant digits.

(originally, nautical) A document (usually containing a complaint or petition) originally with the signatures arranged in a circle, and later often alphabetically, to disguise the order of signing and to indicate that the signatories are collectively responsible for it.
A conference at which participants of similar status discuss and exchange views.
(often, figurative, travel) A trip from one destination to another and then returning to the starting location.
(chiefly, UK, New Zealand, Ireland, Canada, Australia, and) A road junction at which traffic streams circularly around a central island.
A roundhead screw, one with a domed head.
(rail transport) A circular building in which locomotives are housed, sometimes with a turntable. [from 19th c.]
In bookbinding, the shaping of the folded and sewed sheets into a convex form at the back.
A Chinese dried meat product with a light and fluffy texture, made by stewing cuts of pork in a sweetened soy sauce mixture.
(transitive) To completely defeat and force into disorderly retreat (an enemy force, opponent in sport, etc.).

(figuratively) One of multiple methods or approaches to doing something.

(Internet) A device that connects local area networks to form a larger internet by, at minimum, selectively passing those datagrams having a destination IP address to the network which is able to deliver them to their destination; a network gateway.
According to established procedure.
A course of action to be followed regularly; a standard procedure.
(computing) A set of instructions designed to perform a specific task; a subroutine.
A mixture of fat (usually butter) and flour used to thicken sauces and stews.
Any of various carnivorous or scavenging beetles of the family Staphylinidae that are often found in decaying matter and have slender bodies and short wing covers.
A vehicle for exploring extraterrestrial bodies.
A line of objects, often regularly spaced, such as seats in a theatre, vegetable plants in a garden, etc.
(transitive, or, intransitive, nautical) To propel (a boat or other craft) over water using oars.
(linear algebra) A 1×n matrix that represents a vector.
Sorbus aucuparia, the European rowan.
Any of various small deciduous trees or shrubs of genus Sorbus, belonging to the rose family, with pinnate leaves, corymbs of white flowers, and usually with orange-red berries.
(US) A small open boat propelled by oars (by rowing).
(countable) A boisterous person; a brawler.
The action of the verb to row.
Of or relating to a monarch or his (or her) family.
A deep, bright blue colour.
(Scotland, historical) A type of Scottish burgh founded by, or subsequently granted, a royal charter; these were legally abolished in 1975.
The family of the ruling sovereign of a country or state.
(poker) An ace-high straight flush; a hand consisting of the cards A, K, Q, J, 10, of the same suit and the rarest and strongest hand in poker.
A substance secreted by honey bees to aid in the development of immature or young bees, supplied in extra measure to those young that will become queen bees.
An easy or straightforward procedure for achieving a goal; a procedure that requires little effort.
The first-person plural pronoun as traditionally used in formal speech by any royal personage to refer to themselves, most especially a sovereign in their role as the monarch.

Impassioned allegiance to or advocacy of the establishment, maintenance, and/or interests of a particular king, royal house, or kingly dynasty; sometimes extended to the same of a non-royal (i.e., grand ducal, imperial, or other) family or sovereign; often contrasted with monarchism.
The payment received by an owner of real property for exploitation of mineral rights in the property.
(by extension) Payment made to a writer, composer, inventor etc for the sale or use of intellectual property, invention etc.
(transitive) To move (one object) while maintaining contact with another object over some area, with pressure and friction.
(idiomatic) To aggravate or exacerbate a physical or emotional injury.
(uncountable, countable) Pliable material derived from the sap of the rubber tree; a hydrocarbon biopolymer of isoprene.

(countable, baseball) The rectangular pad on the pitcher's mound from which the pitcher must pitch.
(countable, North America, slang) A condom, especially an external condom.
(uncountable, slang) Tires, particularly racing tires.
Ficus elastica, a tropical tree used as a houseplant, native to Asia.
(literally) A piece of rubber or similar material with a design or text carved or molded for the purpose of transferring ink or dye to imprint that design on another object.

(originally, US) A person who rubbernecks; someone who cranes their neck as though it were made of rubber to see something (such as a tourist attraction) or to watch an event (such as an accident); a rubberneck.
An impression of an embossed or incised surface made by placing a piece of paper over it and rubbing with graphite, crayon or other coloring agent.
(chiefly, UK, Ireland, Commonwealth, colloquial) Exceedingly bad; awful.
Used to express that something is exceedingly bad, awful, or terrible.
Used to express that what was recently said is nonsense or untrue; balderdash!, nonsense!
(by extension, chiefly, Commonwealth) Nonsense.
(transitive, chiefly, UK, Ireland, Commonwealth, colloquial) To criticize, to denigrate, to denounce, to disparage. [from c. 1950s (Australia, New Zealand)]
The broken remains of an object, usually rock or masonry.

(uncountable) The chemical element (symbol Rb) with an atomic number of 37. It is a soft, highly reactive alkali metal.
The monetary unit of Russia, Belarus and Transnistria equal to 100 kopeks (Russian: копе́йка, Belarusian: капе́йка). The Russian ruble's symbol is ₽.
(typography) A pronunciation guide written above or beside Chinese characters.
(uncountable, printing, UK, dated) The size of type between pearl and nonpareil, standardized as 5½-point.
(UK, Northeastern US) A bag carried on the back or shoulder, supported by straps.
(nautical) An underwater vane used to steer a vessel. The rudder is controlled by means of a wheel, tiller or other apparatus (modern vessels can be controlled even with a joystick or an autopilot).

(aeronautics) A control surface on the vertical stabilizer of a fixed-wing aircraft or an autogyro. On some craft, the entire vertical stabilizer comprises the rudder. The rudder is controlled by foot-operated control pedals.
A migratory duck, Tadorna ferruginea.
A stout short-billed wading bird in the wader family of Scolopacidae; Arenaria interpres.
Lacking in refinement or civility; bad-mannered; discourteous.
The property of being rude.
(often, _, in the plural) A fundamental principle or skill, especially in a field of learning.
Any of various perennial shrubs of the genus Ruta, especially the herb Ruta graveolens (common rue), formerly used in medicines.
A circular frill or ruffle on a garment, especially a starched, fluted frill at the neck in Elizabethan and Jacobean England (1560s–1620s).

Philomachus pugnax (syn. Calidris pugnax), a gregarious, medium-sized wading bird of Eurasia; specifically, a male of the species which develops a distinctive ruff of feathers and ear tufts during mating season (the female is called a reeve).
(zoology) The connected series of large egg capsules, or oothecae, of several species of American marine gastropods of the genus Fulgur.
Melaniparus rufiventris, a small bird of the tit family Paridae
a passerine bird of the antbird family, Thamnophilus torquatus.
A partial covering for a floor. [1624]

A form of football in which players can hold or kick an ovoid ball; rugby football. The ball cannot be handled forwards and points are scored by touching the ball to the ground in the area past the opponent's territory or by kicking the ball between goalposts and over a crossbar.
A person who plays rugby, especially professionally.
(countable, sometimes, in the plural) The remains of a destroyed or dilapidated construction, such as a house or castle.

To destroy or render something no longer usable or operable.
To upset or overturn the plans or progress of, or to have a disastrous effect on something.
To reveal the ending of (a story); to spoil.
The state of being ruined, a state of devastation or destruction.
The act of ruining or wrecking.
A regulation, law, guideline.
(uncountable) The act of ruling; administration of law; government; empire; authority; control.
(transitive, stative) To regulate, be in charge of, make decisions for, reign over.
(legal, often, capitalized) The doctrine that no individual is above the law and that everyone must answer to it.

Without rules; unregulated.

a pen used in graphic design and calligraphy for drawing precise lines of various thicknesses

sense.def: A pattern of variation in a road's surface designed to alert inattentive drivers to potential danger by causing a tactile vibration and audible rumbling if they veer out of their lane.
The first compartment of the stomach of a cow or other ruminants.
Any artiodactyl ungulate mammal which chews cud in the suborder Ruminantia, such as a cow or deer.

The buttocks.

Act or instance of running, of moving rapidly using the feet.

An enclosure for an animal; a track or path along which something can travel.
A production quantity (such as in a factory).
A flow of liquid; a leak.

To flee by running.

(transitive, idiomatic) To drive over, causing injury or death.

A Finnic or Scandinavian epic poem, or a division of one, especially a division of the Kalevala.

(pejorative) A lackey; a lapdog; an unprincipled person who helps or flatters other, more powerful and often evil people.

(idiomatic) A flamboyant display of military power as an implied threat that it might be used.

(biochemistry, transitive) To convert (soluble polysaccharides) into simple sugars
(chemistry) A white, crystalline powder, C7H5NO3S, used as an artificial sweetener in food products.

A bag; especially a large bag of strong, coarse material for storage and handling of various commodities, such as potatoes, coal, coffee; or, a bag with handles used at a supermarket, a grocery sack; or, a small bag for small items, a satchel.

The bodhi tree, Ficus religiosa, venerated by Buddhists because they believe the Buddha attained enlightenment while sitting underneath such a tree.
Nelumbo nucifera, native in temperate and subtropical Asia, from India to Japan.
A human being or an animal, or a physical object or immaterial thing (see sense 1.3), offered to a deity.
To destroy or surrender (something) for the sake of something else regarded as more urgent or valuable.
(religion) To offer (a human being or an animal, or an object) to a deity.
To destroy or kill (a human being or an animal); specifically (science) , to kill (an animal) for a scientific experiment or test.

Desecration, profanation, misuse or violation of something regarded as sacred.

Feeling sorrow; sorrowful, mournful.

A seat for a rider, typically made of leather and raised in the front and rear, placed on the back of a horse or other animal, and secured by a strap around the animal's body.

To put (something) on to another thing like a saddle on an animal.
Achievement of sexual gratification by inflicting pain or humiliation on others, or watching pain or humiliation inflicted on others.
One who derives pleasure through cruelty or pain to others.

A commercial tourist attraction, similar to a zoo, in which visitors drive through animal enclosures.
Providing protection from danger; providing shelter.

(idiomatic) Having come to no harm, especially after being exposed to danger.

Sexual activity engaged in by people who have taken precautions to protect themselves against sexually transmitted diseases (STDs).
A fireproof metal box, stored in a secure vault, for holding personal valuables

A valve set to open at a pressure below that at which a container holding a gas, vapour, etc. (such as a boiler or pressure cooker), would burst, thus reducing the pressure; a relief valve.

A cultivated thistle-like plant, Carthamus tinctorius, family Asteraceae, now grown mainly for its oil.
Having an orange-yellow colour.
A plant of species Crocus sativus, a crocus.
A spice (seasoning) and colouring agent made from the stigma and part of the style of the plant, sometimes or formerly also used as a dye and insect repellent.
An orange-yellow colour, the colour of a lion's pelt.
Any of various Greek dishes cooked in a small frying pan, especially an appetizer of pan-seared cheese.
Wise.

Any of a number of plants such as sagebrush considered to be similar to Salvia officinalis, mostly because they are small shrubs and have gray foliage or are aromatic.
(historical) Any kind of carrying container hung from one's belt or sash (in Japan), such as a coin purse, tobacco pouch, or pillbox.
A powdered starch obtained from certain palms (Metroxylon spp., esp. Metroxylon sagu), used as a flour and food thickener and for sizing textiles.
Any of the palms and cycads from which sago starch is extracted.
Mentioned earlier; aforesaid.
Saiga tatarica, an antelope which inhabits a vast area between Kalmykia, Kazakhstan, southern Siberia.
(nautical) A piece of fabric attached to a boat and arranged such that it causes the wind to drive the boat along. The sail may be attached to the boat via a combination of mast, spars and ropes.
To ride in a boat, especially a sailboat.
(watercraft) A boat propelled by a sail.
A strong, durable fabric suitable for making sails for ships or boats.
A fish, Arctoscopus japonicus.
A fish of the genus Istiophorus, having a characteristic sail-like fin on its back.

A ship with masts and sails, powered by the wind.
In particular, a member of the crew of a (civilian or military) vessel, as opposed to a captain, admiral, etc.; a mariner; a common seaman.
(religion, generally) A deceased person whom a church or another religious group has officially recognised as especially holy or godly; one eminent for piety and virtue.

Shorea robusta, a dipterocarpaceous tree.

A sauce, such as mayonnaise, used to flavour or season a salad.
Any salak palm (Salacca zalacca), native to Indonesia; also called.

It is marketed under the trademarks Combivent, Proventil and Ventolin.

Piece of sugar in the shape of a cube (or approximate cube), often used for coffee or tea.
(slang) A man who spends money on an often younger romantic or sexual partner in order to maintain the relationship.
Petaurus breviceps, an omnivorous gliding arboreal marsupial, endemic to mainland Australia and New Guinea, and introduced to Tasmania in 1835.
(UK, Irish, Commonwealth, informal) An older woman who spends money on a younger person, usually for romantic or sexual reasons.
A North American hardwood tree, Acer saccharum, famed as the source of maple sugar and maple flavoring; the wood from such a tree.
A food additive that replicates the sweetness of sugar but is not sugar.
Of food, drink, medication, chewing gum, etc: not containing sugar (and usually sweetened with a sugar substitute instead).
(historical) A block of refined sugar, usually in the form of a truncated cone, in which form it was traditionally exported from the Caribbean and Brazil from the 17th century to the 19th century.
Of food, drink, etc, containing or covered with a large amount of sugar.
(transitive) To cause one to suppose (something); to bring to one's mind the idea (of something).
(obsolete, transitive) To seduce; to prompt to evil; to tempt.
(countable) Something suggested (with subsequent adposition being for)
A receptacle with an opening into which people may place slips of paper containing suggestions for improvement, or for similar feedback.
(Islam) A pre-dawn breakfast during the Ramadan fasting.
(countable) A particular instance of a person intentionally killing oneself, or of multiple people doing so.
(countable) A person who has intentionally killed themself.
(figuratively) An action that could cause the literal or figurative death of a person or organization, although death is not the aim of the action.
An attack on others that involves the assailant committing suicide.

One who carries explosives on his or her body or in a vehicle and intends to detonate them (dying in the process) to kill people and inflict widespread damage, usually motivated by a political or religious cause.
An attack carried out by a suicide bomber or a group of them.
A message, usually a written note, left by someone who later attempts or commits suicide, usually explaining the reason for the suicide.

(card games) Each of the sets of a pack of cards distinguished by colour and/or specific emblems, such as the spades, hearts, diamonds, or clubs of traditional Anglo, Hispanic, and French playing cards.
(transitive) To make proper or suitable; to adapt or fit.
(transitive, figurative) To be appropriate or apt for.
Having sufficient or the required properties for a certain purpose or task; appropriate to a certain occasion.
A large (usually rectangular) piece of luggage used for carrying clothes, and sometimes suits, when travelling.
A group of connected rooms, usually separable from other rooms by means of access. [from 18th c.]

(music) An excerpt of instrumental music from a larger work that contains other elements besides the music; for example, the Nutcracker Suite is the music (but not the dancing) from the ballet The Nutcracker, and the Carmen Suite is the instrumental music (but not the singing and dancing) from the opera Carmen.
A Japanese dish of thinly-sliced beef and tofu with dashi, mirin and soy sauce cooked quickly at the table.
A diacritic (ـْ) used in the Arabic abjad to mark the absence of a vowel.
(organic chemistry) Any salt or ester of sulfuric acid.
(organic chemistry) The univalent radical -SH that is the sulfur analogue of hydroxyl and constitutes the thiol group.
(organic chemistry) Any of a class of organic compounds that have a sulfonyl functional group attached to two carbon atoms; drugs of this structure have been used to treat leprosy.
(chemistry) The bivalent radical or functional group -SO2-
(organic chemistry) Any univalent radical derived from a sulfonic acid
(organic chemistry) Any compound of general formula R2S=O.
Of a yellowish green colour, like that of sulfur.

(uncountable) A chemical element (symbol S) with an atomic number of 16, having a bright yellow color and characteristic smell, used commercially in a variety of products such as insecticides, black powder, and matchsticks.
(countable, uncountable) A yellowish green colour, like that of sulfur.

(American spelling, inorganic compound) A toxic gas, of molecular formula SO2 that is found in the emissions of volcanos and those of burning coal or petroleum; dissolves in water to form sulfurous acid and, in the presence of oxygen, sulfuric acid, and is thus responsible for acid rain.
A yellow poisonous mushroom, Hypholoma fasciculare (= Naematoloma fasciculare).
(American spelling, inorganic compound) A transparent, oily liquid, formula H2SO4, that is a strong acid with very many industrial applications.
(inorganic compound) The weak acid, H2SO3, present in a solution of sulfur dioxide in water; it is a reducing agent and mild bleach.
(intransitive) To express ill humor or offence by remaining sullenly silent or withdrawn.
(often, derogatory) silent and withdrawn after being upset
A species of bracket fungus, Laetiporus sulphureus, found in Europe and North America.

A hereditary ruler in various Muslim states (sultanate), varying from petty principalities (as in Yemen), often vassal of a greater ruler, to independent realms, such as Oman, Brunei, Morocco (until 1957) or an empire such as the Turkish Ottoman Empire.
A type of viol, a cither viol.
(weather) Hot and humid; sweltering. [from late 16th c.]
A quantity obtained by addition or aggregation.
A quantity of money.
Any of various shrubs or small trees of the genus Rhus and certain other genera in Anacardiaceae
A sour spice popular in the Eastern Mediterranean, made from the berries of tanner's sumac.
(ambitransitive) To prepare a summary of (something).
Concise, brief, or presented in a condensed form; presenting information in such a form.

One of four seasons, traditionally the second, marked by the longest and typically hottest days of the year due to the inclination of the Earth and thermal lag. Typically regarded as spanning the months of June, July, and August in the Northern Hemisphere and the months of December, January and February in the Southern Hemisphere.
An institution devoted to housing and entertaining children for the summer.
(cuisine) Gỏi cuốn, a Vietnamese roll made of pork, prawn, vegetables, rice vermicelli, and other ingredients wrapped in rice paper.
Any of various academic sessions held in the summer at schools or universities when the usual students are away; either for supplementary or remedial study or as part of distance learning.
(astronomy) The moment when the Earth is in that point of its orbit where the northern or southern hemisphere is most inclined toward the sun.
The period or season of summer.
The highest point of a hill, mountain, or similar geographical feature.
(by extension) An assembly or gathering of the leaders of countries to discuss issues of international significance; also (loosely) , an important or high-level gathering or meeting.
(transitive) To call people together; to convene; to convoke.
(transitive) To ask someone to come; to send for.
A call to do something, especially to come.
(legal) A notice summoning someone to appear in court, as a defendant, juror or witness.
(uncountable) A stylised Japanese form of wrestling in which a wrestler loses if he is forced from the ring, or if any part of his body except the soles of his feet touches the ground.
(countable, colloquial) A rikishi (sumo wrestler).
Magnificent, luxurious, splendid.
(astronomy) A star, especially when seen as the centre of any single solar system.
The light and heat which are received from the sun; sunshine or sunlight.
The star that Earth revolves around, and from which it receives light and heat.
A species of relatively small bears, Helarctos malayanus, found in Southeast Asia.
A bright spot in the sky, usually one of two on a parhelic circle on both sides of the sun (or occasionally above and below it), caused by the refraction of the sun's image through ice crystals.
(climatology) A rain shower which occurs while the sun is shining.
The flowering plant Euphorbia helioscopia.
An upperclassman or senior, in the context of Korea.
A period spent tanning (sunbathing) in the sun.
A visible, narrow, and intense (relative to ambient light) ray of sunlight.
A burn on the skin caused by excess exposure to the sun's rays.
(transitive) To burn or tan (someone's skin) by the sun; to allow (a part of one's body) to become sunburnt.
(originally, US) A dessert consisting of ice cream with various toppings.
Heritiera fomes (syn. H. minor Roxb.); a tree found in high intertidal regions of Bangladesh (especially in Sundarbans), Myanmar, Thailand, etc., with dark durable timber.
Any of a group of insectivorous plants in the genus Drosera that catch insects by sticky droplets ("dew") at the end of hairs on the leaves and grow in boggy ground all over the world.
A device measuring the time of day by the position of a shadow cast by a pole or plate (gnomon) upon an engraved series of marks.

(medicine, psychology, psychiatry) A state of agitation, confusion, or delirium, especially in patients suffering from Alzheimer's disease, which begins daily at nightfall and which is alleviated by daylight.
A typically sleeveless dress, usually a minidress, made of light, loose-fitting material for spring and summer wear.
Any of various large marine fishes of the family Molidae that have an oval compressed body.
A bright yellow, like that of the flower petals.
A vegetable oil, pressed from sunflower seeds, and used in cooking.
Tinted glasses worn to protect the eyes from the sun or other bright light, and may also be worn as a fashion accessory.
(economics) A cost that has already been incurred and which cannot be recovered to any significant degree.
All the electromagnetic radiation given off by the Sun, especially that in the visible spectrum that bathes the Earth.
(figuratively) Brightness, hope; a positive outlook.
A form of extended deckchair used for sunbathing or relaxing (typically by the sea or a pool)
(Islam) (An example of) Muhammad's way of life, as recorded in the hadiths, especially when viewed as a model for Muslims to emulate.
(of weather or a day) Featuring a lot of sunshine.
(US) Of an egg: fried sunny side up.
The time of day when the sun appears above the eastern horizon.
The change in color of the sky at dawn.

(automotive) A fixed or operable opening in a vehicle roof (car or truck) which allows fresh air and/or light to enter the passenger compartment. A sunroof may include a transparent or opaque panel and may be manually operated or power driven.
A topical substance formulated to protect the skin from the harmful effects of ultraviolet radiation by absorbing, reflecting or scattering ultraviolet rays.
The changes in color of the sky before and after sunset.
(figuratively) The final period of the life of a person or thing.
The direct rays, light or warmth of the sun.
(medicine) Heat stroke caused by an excessive exposure to the sun's rays.
A darkening of the skin resulting from exposure to sunlight or similar light sources.
A type of sunscreen that used to attain a suntan.
(psychology) Emptiness, in terms of a meditative state; an Eastern concept of a high meditative state of calm and freedom from distraction.
(musical instruments) A traditional Chinese double-reeded horn with a distinctively loud and high-pitched sound.
Better than average, better than usual; wonderful.

(US politics) A political action committee which may support a political candidate, and officially endorse one, but is legally bound to not coordinate with any candidate, and is not limited in financial contributions from donors or financial spending.
superior in title or status
Any substance having a very high acidity; typically a solution of a strong Lewis acid in a Brønsted acid.
(physics, chemistry) A metamaterial, a cluster of atoms which acts like a single atom. It seems to exhibit some of the properties of elemental atoms.
A large species of songbird, Menura novaehollandiae, family Menuridae, endemic to eastern Australian forests, noted for its lyrate tail feathers and its extraordinary powers of vocal mimicry.
Any high-performance sports car.
(computing, object-oriented programming) A high-level class that passes attributes and methods down the hierarchy to subclasses.
(astronomy) An extended group of clusters of galaxies

cit.quote: スーパーコンピューター

sense.def: (computing) Any computer that has a far greater processing power than others of its generation.
(physics) The property of a material whereby it has no resistance to the flow of an electric current.
A substance that has no resistance to conducting an electric current
(geology) A very large continent that split into smaller ones in the Earth’s geologic past.
(psychoanalysis) The part of the mind that acts as a self-critical conscience, reflecting social standards that have been learnt.
(physics) The frictionless flow that is characteristic of a fluid with zero viscosity, especially liquid helium at temperatures near absolute zero.
In excess of what is required or sufficient.
(astronomy) A very large star having a mass between 10 and 70 solar masses.
(quantum mechanics, relativity) A field theory combining supersymmetry and general relativity.
The heating of a substance above a temperature at which a change of state normally occurs, without it occurring; especially the heating of a liquid above its boiling point.
Any fictional crime-fighting character, often with supernatural powers or equipment, in popular children's and fantasy literature; a fictional hero who does great things.
A heroine with supernatural powers; a female superhero
Beyond what is possible for a human being.
A person who is authorized to supervise, direct or administer something.
Higher in rank, status, or quality.
A person of higher rank or quality, especially a colleague in a higher position.
The state of being superior.
A jet aircraft with some superior quality, such as large size or high speed.

(grammar) The degree of comparison of an adjective or adverb used when comparing three or more entities in terms of a certain property or a certain way of doing something. In English, the superlative of superiority is formed by adding the suffix -est or the word most (e.g. tiniest, most fully); the superlative of inferiority, by adding the word least (e.g. least big, least fully).

(grammar) The degree of comparison of an adjective or adverb used when comparing three or more entities in terms of a certain property or a certain way of doing something. In English, the superlative of superiority is formed by adding the suffix -est or the word most (e.g. biggest, most fully); the superlative of inferiority, by adding the word least (e.g. least big, least fully).
(chiefly, philosophy) An imagined superior type of human being representing a new stage of human development; an übermensch, an overman. [from 1903.]
A man of extraordinary or seemingly superhuman powers.
A chain of such stores.
A highly paid, famous fashion model.
(astrology, astronomy) A full moon or new moon, when the Earth–Moon distance is in the lowest tenth of its range.
Above nature; beyond or added to nature, often so considered because it is given by a deity or some force beyond that with which humans are born.
(star) A powerful and bright explosion of a massive star, which afterwards becomes a neutron star or a black hole, or is destroyed.
(taxonomy) A taxonomic category below subclass and above order.
(mathematics, physics) The principle stating that for a linear system, the net response is the sum of the response associated with each individual input.
(countable) A sovereign state with dominant status on the globe and a very advanced military, especially the United States or formerly the Soviet Union.
(countable, originally, fiction) An extraordinary physical or mental ability, especially possessed by a superhero or supervillain.
Very wealthy people, considered as a class. [from 19th c.]
(chemistry, physics, of a solution) More concentrated than is normally possible.
(physics, of a vapor) Having a vapor pressure higher than is normally possible.
(physiology) The condition of a solution of gases in a tissue having a higher concentration in terms of sum of partial pressures than the ambient pressure.
(typography) A type of lettering form that appears as a number, figure, or symbol above the normal line of type, located at the right or left of another symbol or text.
(set theory) (symbol: ⊇) With respect to another set, a set such that each of the elements of the other set is also an element of the set.
(of a speed) Greater than the speed of sound (in the same medium, and at the same temperature and pressure).
Someone who has accumulated a vast amount of fame; a high-level celebrity.
A belief or beliefs, not based on human reason or scientific knowledge, that events may be influenced by one's behavior in some magical or mystical way.
Susceptible to superstitions.
(physics) a hypothetical object consisting of a very small one-dimensional string that vibrates in ten (or more) dimensions
(Marxism) The social sphere of ideology which includes religion, art, politics, law and all traditional values.
(physics) A theory that attempts to unify the fundamental physical forces and which proposes a physical symmetry between bosons and fermions.
A fantasy-fiction criminal or evil-doer, often with supernatural powers or equipment, in popular children's and fantasy literature who can present a credible challenge for a superhero.
(uncountable) The act or instance of supervising.
(management) A person with the official task of overseeing the work of a person or group, or of other operations and activities.
A woman with superhuman powers.
Food consumed before going to bed.
Any meal eaten in the evening; dinner eaten in the evening, rather than at noon.
Additional; added to supply what is wanted.
(geometry) A pair of angles that sum to 180 degrees.

(linguistics, grammar) The use of an unrelated word or phrase to supply inflected forms otherwise lacking, e.g. using “to be able” as the infinitive of “can”, or “better” as the comparative of “good”, or “went” as the simple past of “go”.
One who supplies; a provider.
(uncountable) The act of supplying.
(countable) An amount of something supplied.
(in the plural) Provisions.
(transitive) To provide (something), to make (something) available for use.
(transitive) To compensate for, or make up a deficiency of.
(transitive) To fill temporarily; to serve as substitute for another in, as a vacant place or office; to occupy; to have possession of.

(economics) A capitalistic model of price determination in a market, according to which, holding all else equal in a competitive market, the unit price for a particular good will eventually settle at a point where the quantity demanded will equal the quantity supplied (at the current price).
A system of organizations, people, technology, activities, information and resources involved in moving a product or service from the supplier to the customer.
(sometimes, attributive) Something which supports.
Financial or other help.
(transitive) To help keep from falling.
(transitive) To help, particularly financially; to subsidize.
(transitive) To answer questions and resolve problems regarding something sold.
(transitive, said of electronic devices, programming languages, etc.) To be designed to provide capacity for; to work or be compatible with (a part, accessory, file type, program, algorithm, etc.).
(transitive, intransitive) To take for granted; to conclude, with less than absolute supporting data; to believe.
(transitive) To theorize or hypothesize.
Something that is supposed; an assumption made to account for known facts, conjecture.
(medicine) A medicine in the form of a small plug that is inserted into a bodily cavity, especially the rectum, vagina or urethra, where it melts at body temperature.
(obsolete) To hold in place, to keep low.
(intransitive) To form or discharge pus.
A small muscle at the top of the shoulder blade.
The quality of being supreme.
Dominant, having power over all others.
A court of law which represents the highest legal authority within a jurisdiction.

(set theory) (real analysis) : Given a subset X of R, the smallest real number that is ≥ every element of X; (order theory) : given a subset X of a partially ordered set P (with partial order ≤), the least element y of P such that every element of X is ≤ y.
Any of the 114 chapters of the Quran.
An addition of extra charge on the agreed, stated, or baseline price.
Physically secure and certain, non-failing, reliable.
Certain in one's knowledge or belief.
(in response to a request for help or a favour) Yes; of course.
Without fail.
(sentence adverb) Certainly, undoubtedly.
To ride a wave on a surfboard; to pursue or take part in the sport of surfing.
The overside or up-side of a flat object such as a table, or of a liquid.
(mathematics, geometry) The locus of an equation (especially one with exactly two degrees of freedom) in a space of more than two dimensions.
(physics) the effect on the surface of a liquid that makes it behave as a stretched elastic membrane; it is caused by unbalanced intermolecular forces
(of a missile) fired from the ground, or from a ship, at an aircraft in flight, or at an incoming missile
(military) A ground-based anti-aircraft missile.
(chemistry) A surface-active agent, or wetting agent, capable of reducing the surface tension of a liquid; typically organic compounds having a hydrophilic “head” and a hydrophobic “tail”.
(biochemistry) A lipoprotein in the tissues of the lung that reduces surface tension and permits more efficient gas transport.
A shaped waterproof plank, usually made of wood or foam and reinforced plastic, used to surf on waves.
The pastime or sport of riding surf on a surfboard.
One who performs surgery; a doctor who performs operations on people or animals.
A knot derived from the reef knot, commonly used by surgeons.
(medicine, usually, _, uncountable) A procedure involving major incisions to remove, repair, or replace a part of a body.
(medicine) The medical specialty related to the performance of surgical procedures.
A room or department where surgery is performed.
(medicine, infectious disease) A mask worn to catch bacteria shed in liquid droplets and aerosols from the wearer's mouth and nose.
A white paste, made from ground fish, that is used to make formed and textured food products.

(set theory) A function for which every element of the codomain is mapped to by some element of the domain; (formally) Any function f: X\rightarrow Y for which for every y \in Y, there is at least one x \in X such that f(x) = y.
(mathematics) Of, relating to, or being a surjection.
(intransitive) To imagine or suspect; to conjecture; to posit with contestable premises.
(transitive) To get or be over without touching or resting on; to overcome.

The portion of a person's name that is generally hereditary or treated as an indicator of a person's family, which may be shared with other members of the family, or otherwise derived from their names in some fashion; distinguished from that person's given name(s).
(transitive) To go beyond or exceed (something) in an adjudicative or literal sense.
That which remains when use or need is satisfied, or when a limit is reached; excess; overplus; overage.
Specifically, an amount in the public treasury at any time greater than is required for the ordinary purposes of the government.
Something unexpected.
The feeling that something unexpected has happened.
(transitive) To cause (someone) to feel unusually alarmed or delighted by something unexpected.
Caused to feel surprise, amazement or wonder, or showing an emotion due to an unexpected event.
In a way that causes surprise because it is unexpected, or unusual.
Resembling a dream: fantastic and incongruous.
(art) An artistic movement and an aesthetic philosophy that aims for the liberation of the mind by emphasizing the critical and imaginative powers of the subconscious.
An act of surrendering, submission into the possession of another; abandonment, resignation.
The yielding or delivery of a possession in response to a demand.
(legal, property law) The yielding of the leasehold estate by the lessee to the landlord, so that the tenancy for years merges in the reversion and no longer exists.
(intransitive, or, reflexive) To give oneself up into the power of another, especially as a prisoner; to submit or give in.
A woman who gives birth to a child with the intent to give this child to at least one of the biological parents (not including herself, if she is one of them)
(transitive) To encircle something or simultaneously extend in all directions.
(transitive) To enclose or confine something on all sides so as to prevent escape.
The area surrounding someone or something, together with the objects and circumstances in the vicinity; the environment or ambiance.

cit.quote: シュールストレミング

sense.def: A traditional Swedish food made by fermenting Baltic herring in wooden casks.
Close observation of an individual or group; person or persons under suspicion.
A mounted video camera used for the purpose of surveillance, as part of closed-circuit television.
A particular view; an examination, especially an official examination, of a particular group of items, in order to ascertain the condition, quantity, or quality.
The operation of finding the contour, dimensions, position, or other particulars of any part of the Earth's surface.

To determine the form, extent, position, etc., of, as a tract of land, a coast, harbor, or the like, by means of linear and angular measurements, and the application of the principles of geometry and trigonometry
To examine and ascertain, as the boundaries and royalties of a manor, the tenure of the tenants, and the rent and value of the same.
A person occupied with surveying: the process of determining positions on the earth's surface.
The fact or act of surviving; continued existence or life.
(anthropology) A custom or belief that persists in folklore from earlier times, when the rationale behind it is forgotten.
A knife intended for survival purposes in a wilderness environment, often in an emergency situation when the user has lost other equipment.
(evolutionary theory) Natural selection.
(intransitive) Of a person, to continue to live; to remain alive.
One who survives, especially one who survives a traumatic experience.
(proscribed) Raw fish, especially as a Japanese dish.
A type of sushi originating in Canada, made from fried rice patties topped with raw seafood and avocado slices and drizzled with condiments.
Any of several large Eurasian squirrels, of the genera Citellus or Spermophilus.
A person who is suspected of something, in particular of committing a crime.
(transitive) To believe (someone) to be guilty.
To halt something temporarily.
To discontinue or interrupt a function, task, position, or event.
To hang freely; underhang.
(science fiction) The deliberate slowing of the body's functions, sometimes by the use of cryonics, on long interstellar journeys.
(sex position, idiomatic) A sex position which consists of one participant carrying the other while penetrating them.
A bridge whose deck or roadway is suspended from cables.
The acceptance of people, for the sake of appreciation of art (including literature and the like), of what they know to be a nonfactual premise of the work of art.
The act of suspecting something or someone, especially of something wrong.
The condition of being suspected.
Uncertainty, doubt.
A trace, or slight indication.
The imagining of something without evidence.
Arousing suspicion.
Distrustful or tending to suspect.
Expressing suspicion

(ecology) A means of configuring civilization and human activity so that society, its members and its economies are able to meet their needs and express their greatest potential in the present, while preserving biodiversity and natural ecosystems, planning and acting for the ability to maintain these necessary resources for future generations.
Able to be sustained.
Able to be produced or sustained for an indefinite period without damaging the environment, or without depleting a resource; renewable.
(agriculture, ecology) Development which seeks to produce sustainable economic growth while ensuring future generations' ability to do the same by not exceeding the regenerative capacity of nature.
Miscanthus sinensis, a species of grass native to eastern Asia, including China, Japan, Taiwan and Korea.
Japanese small okurigana used with kanbun or small kana used for diphthongs.
A rule or thesis in Sanskrit grammar or Hindu law or philosophy.
(Buddhism, Hinduism) A scriptural narrative, especially a discourse of the Buddha.
(botany) The seam at the union of two margins in a plant.
(international, _, politics) A dominant nation or state that has control over the international affairs of a subservient state which otherwise has domestic autonomy.

A relation between states in which a subservient nation has its own government, but is unable to take international action independent of the superior state; a similar relationship between other entities.
A small, migratory bird of the Hirundinidae family with long, pointed, moon-shaped wings and a forked tail which feeds on the wing by catching insects.
(transitive) To cause (food, drink etc.) to pass from the mouth into the stomach; to take into the stomach through the throat. [from 11th c.]
(transitive) To take (something) in so that it disappears; to consume, absorb. [from 13th c.]
(intransitive) To take food down into the stomach; to make the muscular contractions of the oesophagus to achieve this, often taken as a sign of nervousness or strong emotion. [from 18th c.]
A plant of any of several species of plants whose parts resemble a swallow's tail:
The forked tail of a swallow.
A type of tailcoat with two long tapering tails.
Any of various butterflies of the family Papilionidae, many of which have a long extension to each hindwing.

An area of wet (water-saturated), spongy (soft) land, often with trees, generally a rich ecosystem for certain plants and animals but ill-suited for many agricultural purposes. (A type of wetland. Compare marsh, bog, fen.)
Any of various species of large, long-necked waterfowl, of genus Cygnus (bird family: Anatidae), most of which have white plumage.
A novelty swan-shaped boat, associated with tourism and rides for couples/lovers.
A large migratory goose (Anser cygnoides) belonging to the subfamily Anserinae.
(idiomatic) A final performance or accomplishment, especially one before retirement.
An exchange of two comparable things.
(finance) A financial derivative in which two parties agree to exchange one stream of non-normal cashflow against another stream.
A large number of insects, especially when in motion or (for bees) migrating to a new colony.
A mass of people, animals or things in motion or turmoil.

(countable) A cross with arms of equal length all bent halfway along at a 90° angle to the right or to the left, used as a religious symbol by various ancient and modern civilizations, but now mainly seen and used in the West (with arms angled to the right) as a symbol of Nazism and fascism.
(transitive) To cause to incline or swing to one side, or backward and forward; to bias; to turn; to bend; to warp.
(ambitransitive) To use offensive, profane, or obscene language.
A word considered obscene and vulgar or offensive.

Fluid that exits the body through pores in the skin usually due to physical stress and/or high temperature for the purpose of regulating body temperature and removing certain compounds from the circulation.
(intransitive) To emit sweat.
(transitive) To emit, in the manner of sweat.
(anatomy) An exocrine gland found under the skin in mammals for regulating body temperature.
A knitted jacket or jersey, usually of thick wool, worn by athletes before or after exercise.
(chiefly US) A similar garment worn for warmth.
One who sweats (produces sweat).
The production and evaporation of a watery fluid called sweat that is excreted by the sweat glands in the skin of mammals.
(US) Informal cotton trousers, with an elasticated or drawstring waist, used for exercise etc.
A loose shirt, usually made of a knit fleece, for athletic wear and now often used as casual apparel.
A factory or other place of work where pay is low and conditions are poor or even illegal. [from 1892]
A two-piece garment worn during exercise.
Covered in sweat.
(transitive) To clean (a surface) by means of a stroking motion of a broom or brush.
(intransitive) To move through a (horizontal) arc or similar long stroke.
(curling) To brush the ice in front of a moving stone, causing it to travel farther and to curl less.
(idiomatic) To conceal a problem (usually an embarrassing or illegal one) expediently, rather than remedy it thoroughly.
Tasting of sugars.
(wine) Retaining a portion of sugar.
Not of a salty taste.
Of a pleasant smell.
Not decaying, fermented, rancid, sour, spoiled, or stale.
Of a pleasant sound.
Of a pleasing disposition.
Of a helpful disposition.
(mineralogy) Free from excessive unwanted substances like acid or sulphur.
(informal) Very pleasing; agreeable.
